short_description.id: Singa adalah sosok penolak bala dalam mitologi Batak di Sumatra Utara, makhluk pelindung yang digambarkan sebagai campuran manusia, kerbau air, dan buaya atau kadal.
short_description.en: The singa is a protective, evil-averting figure of Batak mythology in North Sumatra, pictured as a blend of human, water buffalo, and crocodile or lizard.

long_description.id: Singa adalah sosok penolak bala dari mitologi orang Batak di Sumatra Utara, Indonesia, yang melambangkan kekuatan pelindung yang baik. Ia digambarkan sebagai campuran manusia, kerbau air, dan buaya atau kadal, selalu berwajah panjang dengan mata besar melotot, hidung tegas, dan janggut panjang berpilin. Singa sering digambarkan hanya kepalanya, kadang seluruh tubuhnya, dan sosok lain seperti dewa pelindung atau leluhur dapat ditampilkan berdiri atau duduk di atas kepalanya.
long_description.en: The singa is an apotropaic figure of the mythology of the Batak people of North Sumatra, Indonesia, representing a benevolent protective power. It combines features of a human, a water buffalo and a crocodile or lizard, always with an elongated face, big bulging eyes, a defined nose and a long spiralling beard. It is often shown as a head alone, sometimes full body, and other figures such as protective deities or ancestors may be shown standing or sitting on its head.

long_description.id: Kata singa berasal dari bahasa Sanskerta yang berarti singa, tetapi dalam bahasa Batak maknanya lebih bersifat magis daripada zoologis: ia tidak melambangkan singa, melainkan Naga atau Boru Saniang Naga, ular air purba dari mitologi Hindu-Buddha. Alasan sosok ini dinamai singa belum sepenuhnya dipahami.
long_description.en: The word singa comes from the Sanskrit for lion, but in Batak its meaning is magical rather than zoological: what it symbolizes is not a lion but the Nāga or Boru Saniang Naga, a primeval water serpent from Hindu-Buddhist mythology. Why this figure came to be called singa is not fully understood.

long_description.id: Sebuah katalog koleksi museum menjelaskan bahwa pahatan singa lazimnya dipasang pada ujung balok penopang utama rumah leluhur dan dimaksudkan melambangkan naga padoha, naga purba raksasa yang ditaklukkan oleh dewi Si Boru Deak Parujar. Bumi dikatakan bertumpu pada punggung naga padoha, sebagaimana rumah Batak secara simbolis bertumpu pada punggung sosok-sosok ini. Arsip foto lapangan mencatat kepala singa/naga sebagai ciri penting rumah Batak Toba yang diukir timbul, juga pada gable depan.
long_description.en: A museum collection catalogue entry explains that singa carvings are customarily attached to the ends of the main support beams of the ancestral house and are meant to represent the naga padoha, an enormous primeval dragon subdued by the goddess Si Boru Deak Parujar. The earth is said to rest on the back of the naga padoha, just as the Batak house symbolically rests on the backs of these figures. A field photo archive records the singa/naga head as a significant feature of Toba-Batak houses, carved in relief, also on the front gable.

long_description.id: Gambar singa diukir pada perkakas rumah tangga, wadah obat, perhiasan, jimat, peti mati kayu, sarkofagus batu, lumbung, dan rumah adat Batak, sehingga menjadi lambang budaya Batak; ukiran singa pada rumah disebut singa ni ruma, dan gorga ulu singa dipasang di puncak gable depan. Wadah pupuk (zat magis), atribut datu (dukun), sering diukir dengan gambar singa. Sumbat kayu wadah ramuan naga morsarang selalu berbentuk singa, kadang dengan sosok lain yang menungganginya, dan wadah serupa versi Karo juga memakai sumbat berukir singa. Penggunaannya sebagai penolak bala mungkin berasal dari masa Hindu-Buddha di tanah Batak sekitar abad kesembilan.
long_description.en: Singa images are carved on household utensils, medicine containers, jewellery, amulets, wooden coffins, stone sarcophagi, barns and Batak traditional houses, making it a symbol of Batak culture; the singa carved on a house is called singa ni ruma, and the gorga ulu singa is placed on top of the front gable. A pupuk (magical substance) container, an attribute of the datu (medicine man), is often carved with a singa. The wooden stopper of the naga morsarang potion container is always shaped as a singa, sometimes with other figures mounting it, and the Karo counterpart vessel also uses a stopper carved with a singa. Its apotropaic use may date from the Hindu-Buddhist period of the Batak around the ninth century.

claims.quote: Singa is an apotropaic figure from the mythology of the Batak people of North Sumatra, Indonesia. The singa represents a benevolent and protective power. The singa is described as "part human, part water buffalo, and part crocodile or lizard". It is variedly represented, but always has an elongated face, with big bulging eyes, a well-defined nose, and long spiraling beard.

statement.id: Singa adalah sosok penolak bala dari mitologi Batak di Sumatra Utara, Indonesia, yang melambangkan kekuatan pelindung yang baik; ia digambarkan sebagai campuran manusia, kerbau air, dan buaya atau kadal, berwajah panjang dengan mata besar melotot, hidung tegas, dan janggut panjang berpilin.
statement.en: The singa is an apotropaic figure of Batak mythology, North Sumatra, Indonesia, representing benevolent protective power; described as part human, part water buffalo and part crocodile or lizard, with an elongated face, bulging eyes, a defined nose and a long spiral beard.

claims.quote: The word singa is derived from the Sanskrit singa, "lion". The Batak term singa has a predominantly magical - rather than zoological - meaning, so it does not symbolize a lion, but Nāga or Boru Saniang Naga, the primeval water serpent from the Hindu-Buddhist mythology.

statement.id: Kata singa berasal dari Sanskerta singa ('singa'); dalam bahasa Batak maknanya magis, bukan zoologis, sehingga tidak melambangkan singa, melainkan Naga atau Boru Saniang Naga, ular air purba mitologi Hindu-Buddha.
statement.en: Singa comes from Sanskrit singa ('lion'); in Batak its meaning is magical, not zoological, symbolizing not a lion but the Nāga or Boru Saniang Naga, the primeval water serpent of Hindu-Buddhist mythology.

claims.quote: Images of singa are carved in various objects such as domestic utensils, medicine containers, jewelries, amulets, wood coffins, stone sarcophagi, barns, and Batak traditional houses. Its frequent use made the singa a symbol of the Batak culture. Carving of singa on a Batak house is called singa ni ruma

statement.id: Gambar singa diukir pada perkakas, wadah obat, perhiasan, jimat, peti mati, sarkofagus, lumbung, dan rumah adat Batak, sehingga menjadi lambang budaya Batak; ukiran pada rumah disebut singa ni ruma.
statement.en: Singa images are carved on utensils, medicine containers, jewellery, amulets, coffins, sarcophagi, barns and Batak houses, making it a Batak cultural symbol; on houses it is called singa ni ruma.

claims.quote: The apotropaic use of a singa may stem from the Hindu-Buddhism period of Batak during the ninth century

statement.id: Penggunaan singa sebagai penolak bala mungkin berasal dari masa Hindu-Buddha di tanah Batak pada abad kesembilan.
statement.en: The singa's apotropaic use may stem from the Hindu-Buddhist period of the Batak in the ninth century.

claims.quote: One of the major features of Hindu-Buddhist architecture in Java and Bali is the ubiquitous kirtimukha over arches and doorways.

statement.id: Salah satu ciri utama arsitektur Hindu-Buddha di Jawa dan Bali adalah hiasan kirtimukha di atas lengkung dan pintu.
statement.en: A major feature of Hindu-Buddhist architecture in Java and Bali is the kirtimukha over arches and doorways.

claims.quote: It is often represented only with its head, but sometimes it may also be represented full body. Other figures - such as other protective deity or ancestral figures - may also be represented standing or sitting on top of the head of the singa.

statement.en: The singa is often shown as a head alone, sometimes full body; other figures such as protective deities or ancestral figures may be shown standing or sitting on its head.

statement.id: Belum sepenuhnya dipahami mengapa nama singa dikaitkan dengan sosok ini.
statement.en: It is not fully understood why the name singa is attributed to this figure.

statement.id: Pada masa gaya Aparajita di awal abad kesembilan, versi Batak dari kirtimukha, yang disebut singhamugam, muncul dalam relief penuh.
statement.en: During the Aparajita style period at the beginning of the ninth century, the Batak version of the kirtimukha, called singhamugam, appeared in full relief.

short_description.id: Nawarupa, atau Byala dalam tradisi Rakhine, adalah makhluk campuran dalam mitologi Myanmar yang tersusun dari sembilan hewan, antara lain gajah, rusa, badak, burung nuri, singa, dan merak.
short_description.en: The nawarupa, or byala in Rakhine tradition, is a chimeric creature of Burmese mythology made of nine animals, including the elephant, deer, rhinoceros, parrot, lion and peafowl.

long_description.id: Nawarupa, yang juga dieja Nawa Rupa dan berarti sembilan wujud, adalah makhluk campuran dalam mitologi Myanmar dan Rakhine (Arakan); di Rakhine ia disebut Byala. Makhluk ini tersusun dari sembilan hewan: berkepala gajah, bermata rusa, bertanduk badak, berlidah dan bersayap burung nuri, bertubuh dan berkaki singa, dan berekor merak.
long_description.en: The nawarupa, also spelt Nawa Rupa and meaning nine forms, is a chimeric creature of Burmese and Rakhine (Arakanese) mythology; in Rakhine it is called the byala. It combines nine animals: an elephant's head, a deer's eyes, a rhinoceros's horns, a parrot's tongue and wings, a lion's body and legs and a peafowl's tail.

long_description.id: Nawarupa dikenal terutama lewat perahu kerajaan. Pada masa raja-raja Konbaung, sosok nawarupa menghiasi sebuah perahu upacara kerajaan, dan perahu Nawarupa dipakai para menteri dan pejabat kerajaan. Sebuah perintah raja menyebut Nawa Rupa sebagai perahu dengan patung hewan sembilan bagian di haluan, bersama Panca Rupa (lima bagian) dan Satta Rupa (tujuh bagian).
long_description.en: The nawarupa is known chiefly through royal barges. Under the Konbaung kings a nawarupa figure adorned a ceremonial royal barge, and the Nawarupa barge was used by the royal ministers and officers. A royal order names the Nawa Rupa as a barge with a nine-part animal figure on its prow, alongside the Panca Rupa (five parts) and the Satta Rupa (seven parts).

long_description.id: Sumber-sumber berbeda dalam menggambarkan susunannya. Satu artikel menyebut hiasan haluan Nawarupa terdiri atas surai karaweik, punuk banteng, ekor ikan ngagyin, gading gajah, belalai makara, tanduk toe naya, sayap burung parkit, dan kaki kuda. Upper Burma Gazetteer, sebaliknya, menggambarkan perahu Nawarupa (juga disebut Nawarasa) yang membawa lima patung Brahma di haluan dan empat di buritan untuk memperingati sembilan Brahma.
long_description.en: Sources differ on its make-up. One article says the Nawarupa figurehead consisted of the mane of a karaweik, the hump of a bull, the tail of a ngagyin fish, elephant tusks, the trunk of a makara, the horns of a toe naya, parakeet wings and horse legs. The Upper Burma Gazetteer, by contrast, describes a Nawarupa (also called Nawarasa) boat carrying five Brahma figures at the bow and four at the stern to commemorate nine Brahmas.

long_description.id: Dalam kisah Rakhine, Byala digambarkan sebagai makhluk perdamaian yang selalu berwajah tersenyum, berkaki empat, dengan lingkaran rambut di leher dan ekor yang indah, serta lambang perdamaian dan kemakmuran. Patungnya didirikan di dekat pagoda sebagai lambang pertanda baik, dan ukiran Byala dalam beragam gaya terlihat di sebagian besar kuil di Mrauk-U. Sebuah patung Byala juga berdiri di taman Viewpoint, Sittwe.
long_description.en: In Rakhine lore the Byala is described as a creature of peace always wearing a smiling face, with four legs, a girdle of hair around the neck and a beautiful tail, and as a symbol of peace and prosperity. Its figure is erected near pagodas as an auspicious symbol, and Byala carvings in a variety of styles appear in most Mrauk-U temples. A Byala statue also stands in the Viewpoint park in Sittwe.

long_description.id: Dalam budaya modern, dua partai politik Rakhine, ALD dan ANP, sama-sama mengklaim Byala sebagai lambang; ALD memakainya pada bendera dan segel barunya, tetapi ANP mengajukan keberatan.
long_description.en: In modern times two Rakhine political parties, the ALD and the ANP, both laid claim to the Byala as an emblem; the ALD used it on its new flag and seal, but the ANP objected.

short_description.id: Duende adalah sosok mirip manusia bertubuh kecil dalam cerita rakyat Iberia dan Amerika Latin, serupa kurcaci atau leprechaun, yang juga dikenal di Filipina sebagai dwende.
short_description.en: The duende is a small humanlike figure of Iberian and Latin American folklore, comparable to dwarves or leprechauns, also known in the Philippines as the dwende.

long_description.id: Duende adalah sosok mirip manusia dalam cerita rakyat, dengan ragam dari budaya Iberia, Ibero-Amerika, dan Amerika Latin, yang sebanding dengan kurcaci, gnome, atau leprechaun. Dalam bahasa Kastilia, kata duende berasal dari singkatan dueñ(o) de casa, yang berarti tuan rumah. Menurut sebuah kamus, kata ini merujuk pada roh dalam cerita rakyat Spanyol, Portugis, dan Filipina, secara harfiah berarti 'hantu' atau 'goblin' dalam bahasa Spanyol, dan diyakini berasal dari frasa dueño de casa. Kata yang sama secara tradisional juga dipakai dalam flamenco dan seni lain untuk daya mistis seorang penampil.
long_description.en: The duende is a humanlike figure of folklore with Iberian, Ibero-American and Latin American variants, comparable to dwarves, gnomes or leprechauns. In Castilian, the word comes from a contraction of dueñ(o) de casa, meaning master of the house. One dictionary says the word refers to a spirit in Spanish, Portuguese and Filipino folklore, literally means 'ghost' or 'goblin' in Spanish, and is believed to derive from the phrase dueño de casa. The same word is also traditionally used in flamenco and other arts for a performer's mystical force.

long_description.id: Cerita rakyat Spanyol kaya akan berbagai jenis duende, dan di beberapa daerah mereka punya nama lain, seperti trasno di Galisia, follet di Katalonia, dan trasgu di Asturias. Salah satu jenisnya, diaño, adalah duende usil yang menjelma kuda, sapi, domba jantan, atau hewan ternak lain, bahkan bayi; mereka aktif di malam hari dan menakuti orang yang berjalan larut malam.
long_description.en: Spanish folklore is rich in kinds of duendes, and in some regions they have other names, such as trasno in Galicia, follet in Catalonia and trasgu in Asturias. One kind, the diaño, is a mischievous duende that takes the form of horses, cows, rams or other domestic animals, even a baby; they are active at night and frighten those out at odd hours.

long_description.id: Sebuah keterangan museum menyebut bahwa pada tahun 1600-an duende dianggap roh yang jatuh bersama Lucifer dari surga; mereka hidup di dunia, menakut-nakuti dan menipu orang, serta menimbun harta tak terhitung di sarang bawah tanah. Pada akhir tahun 1700-an, kaum intelektual Spanyol mengejek kepercayaan rakyat pada duende, dan istilah itu sering dipakai untuk menyebut tokoh agama dalam terbitan satir.
long_description.en: A museum note says that in the 1600s duendes were thought to be spirits that fell with Lucifer from heaven; they lived in the world, frightening and tricking people and amassing untold treasures in underground lairs. By the late 1700s Spanish intellectuals ridiculed popular belief in duendes, and the word was often applied to religious figures in satirical publications.

long_description.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Meksiko dan Amerika Barat Daya, duende adalah makhluk mirip gnome yang tinggal di dalam dinding rumah, terutama dinding kamar anak-anak, dan mencoba memotong kuku kaki anak yang tidak terurus. Kepercayaan pada duende masih ada di kalangan orang Mixtec dan Zapotec di Oaxaca. Di Andes, Peru, penulis kolonial Spanyol menyamakan roh hutan setempat dengan duende.
long_description.en: In the folklore of Mexico and the American Southwest, duendes are gnome-like beings living inside house walls, especially children's bedroom walls, who try to clip the toenails of unkempt children. Belief in duendes persists among the Mixtecs and Zapotecs of Oaxaca. In the Andes of Peru, Spanish colonial chroniclers equated local forest spirits with duendes.

long_description.id: Orang Filipina mengenal dwende, yang tinggal di batu dan gua, pohon tua, bagian rumah yang gelap, atau di sarang semut dan gundukan rayap; yang tinggal di gundukan disebut nunò sa punsó. Dwende dianggap baik atau jahat menurut warnanya, putih atau hitam, dan orang yang menginjaknya dipercaya akan dikutuk. Orang Chamorro di Kepulauan Mariana juga mengenal duende sebagai roh usil berwujud kurcaci yang menyembunyikan anak kecil.
long_description.en: Filipinos know the dwende, which lives in rocks and caves, old trees, dark parts of houses, or in anthills and termite mounds; those in mounds are called nunò sa punsó. Dwendes are seen as good or evil according to their colour, white or black, and those who step on them are believed to be cursed. The Chamorro of the Mariana Islands also know the duende as a mischievous dwarf-like spirit that hides small children.

long_description.id: Dalam penuturan lain tentang Filipina, duwende umumnya digambarkan sebagai lelaki tua ('nuno') setinggi anak kecil yang tinggal di bawah tanah. Duwende dikenal dapat membuat orang yang menyakiti atau menyinggungnya menderita penyakit aneh, tetapi ada pula cerita bahwa orang yang berhasil berteman dengannya akan hidup berhasil, dan ada Itim na Duwende yang jahat dan ditakuti. Penulis artikel itu menyebut bahwa orang Spanyol dengan cepat menerapkan istilah 'duende' kepada makhluk-makhluk ini.
long_description.en: In another account of the Philippines, the duwende is commonly described as an old man ('nuno') the height of a small child dwelling beneath the earth. Duwendes are known to make those who hurt or offend them suffer unusual diseases, yet some stories say that anyone who befriends one will have a successful life, and there are also the evil and dreaded Itim na Duwende. The author notes that the Spanish were quick to apply the term 'duende' to these beings.

statement.en: The duende is a humanlike folklore figure from Iberian, Ibero-American and Latin American cultures, comparable to dwarves, gnomes or leprechauns.

claims.quote: In Castilian, duende originated as a contraction of the phrase dueñ(o) de casa, effectively "master of the house"

statement.id: Dalam bahasa Kastilia, duende berasal dari singkatan dueñ(o) de casa, 'tuan rumah'.
statement.en: In Castilian, duende comes from a contraction of dueñ(o) de casa, 'master of the house'.

claims.quote: In some regions of Spain, duendes may have other names like Trasnos in Galicia, Follets in Catalonia, Iratxoak in the Basque Country and Navarra, Trasgus in Asturias

statement.id: Di beberapa daerah Spanyol, duende disebut trasno (Galisia), follet (Katalonia), iratxo (Basque dan Navarra), atau trasgu (Asturias).
statement.en: In parts of Spain, duendes are called trasnos (Galicia), follets (Catalonia), iratxoak (Basque Country and Navarra) or trasgus (Asturias).

claims.quote: Busgosos, also known as musgosos, are tall bearded duendes dressed in moss and leaves. They play sad songs on their flutes to help guide shepherds through forests.

statement.id: Busgoso atau musgoso adalah duende tinggi berjanggut berpakaian lumut dan daun yang meniup seruling untuk menuntun gembala di hutan.
statement.en: Busgosos or musgosos are tall bearded duendes in moss and leaves who play flutes to guide shepherds through forests.

claims.quote: Diaños are mischievous duendes that adopt the figure of horses, cows, rams or any other domestic animal, even a human baby. They are active during the night, scaring those who walk at odd hours

statement.id: Diaño adalah duende usil yang menjelma kuda, sapi, domba jantan, hewan ternak lain, atau bayi; mereka aktif malam hari dan menakuti orang yang berjalan larut malam.
statement.en: Diaños are mischievous duendes taking the form of horses, cows, rams, other farm animals or a baby; active at night, they scare late walkers.

claims.quote: In the Hispanic folklore of Mexico and the American Southwest, duendes are known as gnome-like creatures who live inside the walls of homes, especially in the bedroom walls of young children. They attempt to clip the toenails of unkempt children, often leading to the mistaken removal of entire toes. Belief in duendes still exists among the Mixtecs and Zapotecs of Oaxaca

statement.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Meksiko dan Amerika Barat Daya, duende adalah makhluk mirip gnome di dalam dinding rumah, terutama kamar anak, yang mencoba memotong kuku kaki anak tak terurus hingga kadang terpotong seluruh jarinya; kepercayaan ini masih ada di kalangan Mixtec dan Zapotec di Oaxaca.
statement.en: In Mexican and American Southwest folklore, duendes are gnome-like beings in house walls, especially children's rooms, who clip unkempt children's toenails, sometimes removing whole toes; belief persists among Oaxaca's Mixtecs and Zapotecs.

claims.quote: Filipino people have folklore telling of the dwende, which often dwell in rocks and caves, old trees, unvisited and dark parts of houses, or in anthills and termite mounds. Those that live in the last two are termed nunò sa punsó (Tagalog for "old man of the mound"). They are either categorized as good or evil depending on their color (white or black, respectively)

statement.id: Cerita rakyat Filipina mengenal dwende yang tinggal di batu, gua, pohon tua, bagian rumah yang gelap, atau sarang semut dan gundukan rayap (disebut nunò sa punsó, 'kakek gundukan'); mereka baik atau jahat menurut warnanya, putih atau hitam.
statement.en: In the Philippines, folklore tells of the dwende living in rocks, caves, old trees, dark parts of houses, or anthills and termite mounds (called nunò sa punsó, 'old man of the mound'); they are good or evil by colour, white or black.

claims.quote: Offending a nunò sa punsó is taboo; people who step on them are believed to be cursed by the angered dwende within.

statement.id: Menyinggung nunò sa punsó adalah tabu; orang yang menginjaknya dipercaya dikutuk dwende yang marah.
statement.en: Offending a nunò sa punsó is taboo; those who step on one are believed cursed by the angry dwende.

claims.quote: is a goblin, elf, ghost, or spook in the form of a dwarf, a mischievous spirit which hides or takes small children. Some believe the Duende to be helpful or shy creatures, while others believe them to be mischievous and eat misbehaving children.

statement.id: Menurut kamus Chamorro-Inggris, duende adalah goblin atau roh usil berwujud kurcaci yang menyembunyikan atau mengambil anak kecil; sebagian percaya ia penolong atau pemalu, sebagian lagi menganggapnya usil dan memakan anak nakal.
statement.en: Per a Chamorro-English dictionary, the duende is a goblin or mischievous dwarf-like spirit that hides or takes small children; some see it as helpful or shy, others as mischievous and eating naughty children.

claims.quote: In the Andean region of Peru, early colonial accounts recorded local beliefs in forest spirits that Spanish chroniclers equated with duendes or succubi.

claims.quote: The Chamorro people of the Marianas Islands tell tales of the taotaomo'na, duendes and other spirits.

statement.id: Orang Chamorro di Kepulauan Mariana bercerita tentang taotaomo'na, duende, dan roh lainnya.
statement.en: The Chamorro of the Mariana Islands tell of the taotaomo'na, duendes and other spirits.

claims.quote: In the 1600s, duendes (hobgoblins) were thought to be spirits that fell with Lucifer from heaven. Instead of going to hell, they lived in the world, where they frightened and tricked people and amassed untold treasures that they hid in underground lairs.

statement.id: Pada tahun 1600-an, duende dianggap roh yang jatuh bersama Lucifer dari surga; alih-alih ke neraka, mereka hidup di dunia, menakut-nakuti dan menipu orang, serta menimbun harta tak terhitung di sarang bawah tanah.
statement.en: In the 1600s, duendes (hobgoblins) were thought to be spirits that fell with Lucifer from heaven; instead of going to hell they lived in the world, frightening and tricking people and amassing untold treasures hidden in underground lairs.

claims.quote: By the late 1700s, Spanish intellectuals ridiculed the populace’s belief in duendes. The term was often used to refer to religious figures in satirical publications.

statement.id: Pada akhir tahun 1700-an, kaum intelektual Spanyol mengejek kepercayaan rakyat pada duende, dan istilah itu sering dipakai untuk menyebut tokoh agama dalam terbitan satir.
statement.en: By the late 1700s, Spanish intellectuals ridiculed popular belief in duendes, and the term was often used to refer to religious figures in satirical publications.

claims.quote: The word duende refers to a spirit in Spanish, Portuguese, and Filipino folklore and literally means "ghost" or "goblin" in Spanish. It is believed to derive from the phrase dueño de casa, which means "owner of a house."

statement.id: Kata duende merujuk pada roh dalam cerita rakyat Spanyol, Portugis, dan Filipina, dan dalam bahasa Spanyol secara harfiah berarti 'hantu' atau 'goblin'; diyakini berasal dari frasa dueño de casa, 'pemilik rumah'.
statement.en: The word duende refers to a spirit in Spanish, Portuguese and Filipino folklore and literally means 'ghost' or 'goblin' in Spanish; it is believed to derive from the phrase dueño de casa, 'owner of a house'.

claims.quote: The term is traditionally used in flamenco music or other art forms to refer to the mystical or powerful force given off by a performer to draw in the audience.

statement.id: Istilah ini secara tradisional juga dipakai dalam musik flamenco dan seni lain untuk menyebut daya mistis atau kuat yang dipancarkan seorang penampil untuk memikat penonton.
statement.en: The term is traditionally also used in flamenco music and other art forms for the mystical or powerful force a performer gives off to draw in the audience.

cultural_context.en: A musical instrument collection's catalog calls the pyinsarupa an important cultural symbol in Myanmar, and its features are said to symbolize a combination of land, water and winged creatures.

description.id: Dalam zodiak Myanmar, lambang Ketu disebut Hewan Lima Keindahan bernama pyinsarupa, dengan tanduk rusa, gading dan belalai gajah, surai singa, tubuh ular naga, dan ekor ikan.
description.en: In the Burmese zodiac, Ketu's sign is called an Animal of Five Beauties named pyinsarupa, with a deer's antlers, an elephant's tusks and trunk, a lion's mane, a naga serpent's body and a fish's tail.

description.id: Kepala tongkang kerajaan untuk para permaisuri utama berupa pyinsarupa dengan surai burung karaweik, gading dan belalai gajah, punuk sapi, ekor ikan ngagyin, dan tanduk toe naya.
description.en: The royal barge of the chief queens carried a pyinsarupa figurehead with the mane of a karaweik bird, an elephant's tusk and trunk, a bull's hump, a ngagyin fish's tail and the horns of a toe naya.

description.id: Pada masa dinasti Konbaung ada beberapa jenis tongkang kerajaan yang dibedakan oleh kepala mitosnya; salah satunya berkepala pyinsarupa dan dipakai para permaisuri utama.
description.en: By the Konbaung dynasty there were several types of royal barges distinguished by mythical figureheads; one carried a pyinsarupa and was used by the chief queens.

note.id: Makhluk hewan campuran lain dalam cerita Myanmar, tersusun dari sembilan hewan.

short_description.id: Pyinsarupa adalah hewan campuran dalam mitologi Myanmar yang tersusun dari ciri lima hewan, tampil pada gendang hsaing waing dan kepala tongkang kerajaan, serta kini menjadi logo sebuah maskapai.
short_description.en: The pyinsarupa is a chimeric animal of Burmese mythology made of features of five animals, shown on hsaing waing drums and royal barge figureheads and now the logo of an airline.

long_description.id: Pyinsarupa, dari kata Pali pañcarūpa, adalah hewan campuran dalam mitologi Myanmar; dalam bahasa Thai ia disebut phaya luang. Satu sumber menyusunnya dari gajah, sapi jantan, kuda, ikan karper putih, dan tonaya (singa-naga bertanduk dalam mitos), sedangkan versi lain mengganti bahan-bahan itu dengan singa, gajah, kerbau, karper putih, dan hamsa.
long_description.en: The pyinsarupa, from the Pali pañcarūpa, is a chimeric animal of Burmese mythology; in Thai it is called phaya luang. One source composes it from an elephant, bullock, horse, white carp and tonaya (a mythical horned leodragon), while another telling swaps in a lion, elephant, water buffalo, white carp and hamsa.

long_description.id: Sumber lain memberi rincian yang berbeda. Katalog koleksi alat musik menyebut belalai gajah, badan sapi atau kerbau, kaki dan telinga kuda, ekor dan sisik ikan karper, serta sayap hamsa, dan menyebut gabungan itu melambangkan makhluk darat, air, dan bersayap. Dalam zodiak Myanmar, lambang Ketu adalah Hewan Lima Keindahan bernama pyinsarupa, dengan tanduk rusa, gading dan belalai gajah, surai singa, tubuh ular naga, dan ekor ikan.
long_description.en: Other sources give different details. A musical instrument collection's catalog lists an elephant's trunk, a bullock's or buffalo's body, a horse's legs and ears, a carp's tail and scales and a hamsa's wings, and says the combination symbolizes land, water and winged creatures. In the Burmese zodiac, Ketu's sign is an Animal of Five Beauties named pyinsarupa, with a deer's antlers, an elephant's tusks and trunk, a lion's mane, a naga serpent's body and a fish's tail.

long_description.id: Pyinsarupa tampil dalam benda dan upacara kerajaan serta musik. Pada masa dinasti Konbaung ada beberapa jenis tongkang kerajaan yang dibedakan oleh kepala mitosnya, dan satu di antaranya, berlapis emas, dipakai para permaisuri utama dengan kepala pyinsarupa. Gendang besar pat ma gyi dalam ansambel hsaing waing digantung pada rangka tiang yang menggambarkan pyinsarupa, dan sebuah harpa Myanmar dalam sebuah koleksi berbentuk pyinsarupa serta dihias mika, kaca, dan sepuhan emas.
long_description.en: The pyinsarupa appears in royal objects and in music. By the Konbaung dynasty there were several types of royal barges distinguished by their mythical figureheads, and one of them, a gilt barge, was used by the chief queens with a pyinsarupa figurehead. The big pat ma gyi drum of the hsaing waing ensemble is suspended from a pole frame depicting a pyinsarupa, and a Burmese harp in one collection is shaped like a pyinsarupa and decorated with mica, glass and gilt.

long_description.id: Pada masa kini pyinsarupa menjadi logo Myanmar Airways International, dan ia sering tampil dalam orkestra tradisional hsaing waing.
long_description.en: Today the pyinsarupa is the logo of Myanmar Airways International, and it is commonly featured in traditional hsaing waing orchestras.

claims.quote: Pyinsarupa (Burmese: ပဉ္စရူပ, [pjɪ̀ɴsa̰ jùpa̰], also spelt pyinsa rupa; Pali: pañcarūpa

statement.id: Pyinsarupa (ပဉ္စရူပ, juga pyinsa rupa; Pali pañcarūpa, 'lima wujud'), juga dikenal sebagai phaya luang (bahasa Thai), adalah hewan campuran dalam mitologi Myanmar.
statement.en: The pyinsarupa (ပဉ္စရူပ, also pyinsa rupa; Pali pañcarūpa, 'five forms'), also known in Thai as phaya luang, is a chimeric animal of Burmese mythology.

claims.quote: The Pyinsarupa is made of parts of an elephant, a bullock, a horse, a white carp (ငါးကြင်း) and a tonaya (တိုးနရား, a mythical horned leodragon), or alternately a lion, an elephant, a water buffalo, a white carp, and a hamsa.

statement.id: Pyinsarupa tersusun dari bagian gajah, sapi jantan, kuda, ikan karper putih, dan tonaya (singa-naga bertanduk), atau dalam versi lain singa, gajah, kerbau, karper putih, dan hamsa.
statement.en: The pyinsarupa combines an elephant, bullock, horse, white carp and tonaya (a horned leodragon), or alternately a lion, elephant, water buffalo, white carp and hamsa.

claims.quote: The creature is commonly featured in traditional Burmese hsaing waing orchestras, and serves as the logo of Myanmar's flagship air carrier, Myanmar Airways International.

statement.id: Makhluk ini sering tampil dalam orkestra tradisional Myanmar hsaing waing dan menjadi logo maskapai unggulan Myanmar, Myanmar Airways International.
statement.en: It features in traditional Burmese hsaing waing orchestras and is the logo of Myanmar's flagship airline, Myanmar Airways International.

claims.quote: The ‘Pyinsarupa’ is a chimeric animal from Burmese mythology, meaning an amalgamation of the physical characteristics of five different animals, symbolizing a combination of land, water, and winged creatures.

statement.id: Pyinsarupa adalah hewan campuran dari mitologi Myanmar yang menggabungkan ciri fisik lima hewan berbeda, melambangkan gabungan makhluk darat, air, dan bersayap.
statement.en: The pyinsarupa is a chimeric animal of Burmese mythology that combines physical features of five different animals, symbolizing a combination of land, water and winged creatures.

claims.quote: The components of this ‘Pyinsarupa’ consist of the Elephant (trunk); Bullock/Water Buffalo (body); Horse (legs and ears); White Carp/Nga Gyin Fish (tail and scales); and Hamsa (wings).

statement.id: Menurut katalog koleksi ini, komponen pyinsarupa adalah gajah (belalai), sapi jantan atau kerbau (badan), kuda (kaki dan telinga), ikan karper putih atau nga gyin (ekor dan sisik), dan hamsa (sayap).
statement.en: According to this collection catalog, the pyinsarupa's components are the elephant (trunk), bullock or water buffalo (body), horse (legs and ears), white carp or nga gyin fish (tail and scales) and hamsa (wings).

visual_requirements.description: A LIVING BURMESE PYINSARUPA using the specific museum-catalog c05 FIVE-PART variant: ELEPHANT TRUNK at one head, BULL/WATER-BUFFALO BODY, exactly FOUR HORSE LEGS with hooves and HORSE EARS, WHITE CARP/FISH TAIL and pearly white CARP SCALES along rear body, TWO feathered HAMSA GOOSE WINGS at shoulders (c05). short_description.id: Red Boy (Hong Hai-er) adalah siluman muda dalam novel Journey to the West, putra Bull Demon King dan Princess Iron Fan. Ia menguasai api sanmei zhenhuo sebelum ditundukkan Guanyin dan dijadikan Shancai Tongzi.
short_description.en: Red Boy (Hong Hai-er) is a young demon in the novel Journey to the West, the son of Bull Demon King and Princess Iron Fan. He wields the sanmei zhenhuo fire before Guanyin subdues him and names him Shancai Tongzi.

long_description.id: Red Boy adalah tokoh sastra dari novel abad ke-16 Journey to the West (Perjalanan ke Barat). Ia putra Bull Demon King dan Princess Iron Fan, yang menurut Wikipedia seorang Rakshasa. Dalam novel ia dikenal dengan gelar Shengying Dawang (聖嬰大王, Boy Sage Great King) dan tinggal di Huoyun Dong, sebuah gua di Gunung Hao.
long_description.en: Red Boy is a literary character from the 16th-century novel Journey to the West. He is the son of Bull Demon King and Princess Iron Fan, who according to Wikipedia is a Rakshasa. In the novel he is known by the title Shengying Dawang (聖嬰大王, Boy Sage Great King) and lives at Huoyun Dong, a cave on Mount Hao.

long_description.id: Menurut novel, ia berlatih di Flaming Mountain hingga menguasai sanmei zhenhuo, api yang tak bisa dipadamkan hujan Dragon King, dan diutus ayahnya menjaga Gunung Hao. Ia mendengar bahwa memakan daging Tang Sanzang memberi umur panjang, lalu menyamar sebagai anak yang tergantung di pohon pinus untuk memancing rombongan itu. Ia juga menyamar sebagai Guanyin untuk menjebak Zhu Bajie.
long_description.en: According to the novel, he trained on the Flaming Mountain until he mastered sanmei zhenhuo, a fire that the Dragon King's rain cannot put out, and was sent by his father to guard Mount Hao. He heard that eating the flesh of Tang Sanzang grants long life and disguised himself as a child hung in a pine tree to lure the party. He also disguised himself as Guanyin to trap Zhu Bajie.

long_description.id: Sun Wukong mengundang Guanyin, yang kemudian menaklukkannya. Sang Bodhisattva mencukur kepalanya, menyebutnya Shancai Tongzi, dan memasangkan gelang emas padanya karena ia bersikap kurang ajar. Wikipedia mencatat pula bahwa beberapa agama rakyat daerah menghormatinya sebagai dewa, dengan patung di sebuah gua di Meishan.
long_description.en: Sun Wukong invites Guanyin, who then subdues him. The Bodhisattva shaves his head, names him Shancai Tongzi, and fastens a golden band on him because he is disrespectful. Wikipedia also notes that some regional folk religions venerate him as a deity, with a statue in a cavern at Meishan.

cultural_context.id: Wikipedia mencatat bahwa beberapa agama rakyat daerah menghormati Red Boy sebagai dewa; di sebuah gua di Meishan, Provinsi Sichuan, patungnya menjadi objek pemujaan setempat.
cultural_context.en: Wikipedia notes that some regional folk religions venerate Red Boy as a deity; in a cavern at Meishan, Sichuan Province, a statue of him is an object of local worship.

claims.quote: 他曾在火燄山修行了三百年，煉成三昧真火，卻也神通廣大，牛魔王使他來鎮守號山。

statement.id: Dalam novel, dikatakan bahwa Red Boy berlatih tiga ratus tahun di Flaming Mountain (火燄山), menguasai sanmei zhenhuo (三昧真火), berkesaktian besar, dan diutus Bull Demon King (牛魔王) menjaga Gunung Hao (號山).
statement.en: In the novel it is said that Red Boy trained for three hundred years on the Flaming Mountain (火燄山), mastered sanmei zhenhuo (三昧真火), has great powers, and was sent by Bull Demon King (牛魔王) to guard Mount Hao (號山).

claims.quote: 師徒們正當悚懼，又只見那山凹裡有一朵紅雲，直冒到九霄空內，結聚了一團火氣。

statement.id: Dalam novel, saat para peziarah melewati gunung itu, awan merah naik dari lembah hingga ke langit dan menggumpal menjadi hawa api.
statement.en: In the novel, as the travelers cross the mountain, a red cloud rises from the hollow into the sky and gathers into a mass of fire.

claims.quote: 卻說紅光裡，真是個妖精。他數年前聞得人講：東土唐僧往西天取經，乃是金蟬長老轉生，十世修行的好人，有人吃他一塊肉，延生長壽，與天地同休。

statement.id: Dalam novel, makhluk di dalam cahaya merah itu adalah seorang yaojing (妖精, siluman). Ia mendengar bahwa Tang Sanzang (唐僧), yang bepergian ke Barat untuk mengambil kitab, adalah reinkarnasi Jinchan Zhanglao (金蟬長老), dan bahwa orang yang memakan sepotong dagingnya akan hidup panjang.
statement.en: In the novel, the being in the red light is a yaojing (妖精, demon). He has heard that Tang Sanzang (唐僧), traveling west to fetch scriptures, is the reincarnation of Jinchan Zhanglao (金蟬長老), and that anyone who eats a piece of his flesh will live long.

claims.quote: 好妖怪，即散紅光，按雲頭落下。去那山坡裡，搖身一變，變作七歲頑童，赤條條的身上無衣，將麻繩綑了手足，高吊在那松樹梢頭，口口聲聲只叫：「救人，救人！」

statement.id: Dalam novel, Red Boy berubah wujud (搖身一變) menjadi anak berusia tujuh tahun yang telanjang, tangan dan kakinya diikat tali rami dan digantung di pucuk pohon pinus sambil berteriak minta tolong.
statement.en: In the novel, Red Boy transforms (搖身一變) into a seven-year-old child, naked, hands and feet bound with hemp rope and hung from the top of a pine tree, shouting for help.

claims.quote: 有那一夥管兵器的小妖，著兩個擡出一桿丈八長的火尖槍，遞與妖王。妖王掄槍拽步，也無甚麼盔甲，只是腰間束一條錦繡戰裙，赤著腳，走出門前。

statement.id: Dalam novel, Red Boy keluar bertarung membawa tombak ujung api (火尖槍) sepanjang satu zhang delapan chi, tanpa baju zirah, hanya mengenakan rok perang bersulam dan bertelanjang kaki.
statement.en: In the novel, Red Boy comes out to fight with a fire-tipped spear (火尖槍) eighteen chi long, wearing no armor, only an embroidered war skirt, and barefoot.

claims.quote: 將近行到門前，見有一座石碣，上鐫八個大字，乃是「號山枯松澗火雲洞」。

statement.id: Dalam novel, gua tempat tinggal Red Boy berada di Gunung Hao (號山), di Lembah Pinus Kering (枯松澗), dan bernama Huoyun Dong (火雲洞).
statement.en: In the novel, Red Boy's cave lies on Mount Hao (號山), at the Withered Pine Ravine (枯松澗), and is named Huoyun Dong (火雲洞).

claims.quote: 原來龍王私雨，只好潑得凡火，妖精的三昧真火如何潑得？好一似火上澆油，越潑越灼。

statement.id: Dalam novel, hujan yang dikirim Dragon King (龍王) hanya bisa memadamkan api biasa, bukan sanmei zhenhuo (三昧真火) milik siluman itu; hujan justru membuat api makin membara.
statement.en: In the novel, the rain sent by the Dragon King (龍王) can only put out ordinary fire, not the demon's sanmei zhenhuo (三昧真火); it only makes the fire burn the fiercer.

claims.quote: 是我假變觀音，把豬八戒賺來，見吊在如意袋中，也要蒸他與眾小的們吃哩。

statement.id: Dalam novel, Red Boy sendiri mengatakan bahwa ia menyamar sebagai Guanyin (觀音) untuk memancing Zhu Bajie (豬八戒), yang kini tergantung di dalam kantong.
statement.en: In the novel, Red Boy himself says that he disguised himself as Guanyin (觀音) to lure Zhu Bajie (豬八戒), who now hangs in a bag.

claims.quote: 孫大聖十分歡喜，請觀音出了潮音仙洞。諸天大神都列在普陀巖上。菩薩道：「悟空，過海。」

statement.id: Dalam novel, Sun Wukong dengan gembira mengundang Guanyin (觀音) keluar dari gua Chaoyin (潮音仙洞); para dewa berjajar di batu karang Putuo (普陀巖), dan sang Bodhisattva (菩薩) berkata kepadanya, "Wukong, seberangi laut."
statement.en: In the novel, Sun Wukong gladly invites Guanyin (觀音) out of the Chaoyin cave (潮音仙洞); the gods line up on the Putuo rock (普陀巖), and the Bodhisattva (菩薩) says to him, "Wukong, cross the sea."

claims.quote: 菩薩道：「既如此，我與你摩頂受戒。」就袖中取出一把金剃頭刀兒，近前去，把那怪分頂剃了幾刀，剃作一個太山壓頂，與他留下三個頂搭，挽起三個窩角揪兒。

statement.id: Dalam novel, setelah Red Boy memohon ampun, sang Bodhisattva (菩薩) mencukur kepalanya dengan pisau emas hingga berbentuk "太山壓頂" dan menyisakan tiga jambul.
statement.en: In the novel, after Red Boy begs for mercy, the Bodhisattva (菩薩) shaves his head with a golden razor into a "Mount Tai pressing down" (太山壓頂) style, leaving three tufts.

claims.quote: 菩薩道：「你今既受我戒，我卻也不慢你，稱你做善財童子，如何？」那妖點頭受持，只望饒命。

statement.id: Dalam novel, sang Bodhisattva menyebutnya Shancai Tongzi (善財童子) setelah ia menerima ajaran; Red Boy mengangguk menerimanya dengan harapan diampuni.
statement.en: In the novel, the Bodhisattva names him Shancai Tongzi (善財童子) after he accepts the precepts; Red Boy nods and accepts, hoping to be spared.

claims.quote: 卻又袖中取出一個金箍兒來道：「這寶貝原是我佛如來賜我往東土尋取經人的金、緊、禁三個箍兒。緊箍兒先與你戴了；禁箍兒收了守山大神；這個金箍兒未曾捨得與人，今觀此怪無禮，與他罷。

statement.id: Dalam novel, sang Bodhisattva mengeluarkan sebuah gelang emas (金箍兒), satu dari tiga gelang pemberian Buddha, karena Red Boy bersikap kurang ajar, lalu memutuskan memberikannya kepadanya.
statement.en: In the novel, the Bodhisattva takes out a golden band (金箍兒), one of three bands given by the Buddha, and, finding Red Boy disrespectful, decides to give it to him.

claims.quote: 這妖精是牛魔王的兒子，我與他父親相識，若論將起來，還是他老叔哩，他怎敢害我師父？

statement.id: Dalam novel, Sun Wukong berkata bahwa ia mengenal ayah siluman itu, putra Bull Demon King (牛魔王), sehingga secara kekerabatan ia adalah pamannya.
statement.en: In the novel, Sun Wukong says he knows the demon's father, the son of Bull Demon King (牛魔王), so by relation he is his uncle.

claims.quote: In certain regional folk religions, Red Boy is venerated as a deity. A cavern in Meishan, Sichuan Province, houses a statue of Red Boy that serves as an object of local worship.

statement.id: Menurut Wikipedia, dalam agama rakyat di beberapa daerah Red Boy dihormati sebagai dewa; sebuah gua di Meishan, Provinsi Sichuan, menyimpan patungnya yang menjadi objek pemujaan setempat.
statement.en: According to Wikipedia, in certain regional folk religions Red Boy is venerated as a deity; a cavern in Meishan, Sichuan Province, houses a statue of him that serves as an object of local worship.

claims.quote: The 2021 film The Journey to the West: Demon's Child features Red Boy as the main character.

statement.id: Film The Journey to the West: Demon's Child tahun 2021 menampilkan Red Boy sebagai tokoh utama.
statement.en: The 2021 film The Journey to the West: Demon's Child features Red Boy as the main character.

text.id: Tokoh novel Journey to the West; sudah muncul kembali dalam sekuel dinasti Ming
text.en: Character of the novel Journey to the West; reincarnated in a Ming dynasty sequel

short_description.id: Six-Eared Macaque (Liu'er Mihou) adalah kera spiritual dalam novel Journey to the West yang menyamar sebagai Sun Wukong dengan sangat mirip. Ia dikenali Buddha lalu dibunuh Sun Wukong.
short_description.en: The Six-Eared Macaque (Liu'er Mihou) is a spiritual monkey in the novel Journey to the West who impersonates Sun Wukong so closely that none can tell them apart. The Buddha identifies him and Sun Wukong then kills him.

long_description.id: Six-Eared Macaque (六耳獼猴) adalah tokoh sastra dari novel Journey to the West (Perjalanan ke Barat) karya Wu Cheng'en, yang oleh Wikipedia disebut antagonis utama dan paling diingat karena menirukan Sun Wukong. Dalam novel, Rulai (Buddha) menyebutnya satu dari empat kera yang tidak termasuk sepuluh golongan makhluk, dan ia pandai mendengar, mampu menelaah, tahu sebelum dan sesudah, serta memahami segala hal.
long_description.en: The Six-Eared Macaque (六耳獼猴) is a literary character from the novel Journey to the West by Wu Cheng'en, called by Wikipedia a major antagonist and best remembered for impersonating Sun Wukong. In the novel, Rulai (the Buddha) names him one of four monkeys outside the ten categories of beings, skilled at listening, able to discern reason, knowing before and after, and understanding all things.

long_description.id: Menurut ringkasan Wikipedia, ia berharap menggantikan Sun Wukong dan menerima ganjarannya dari Buddha. Ia muncul menyamar sebagai Sun Wukong, membuat Tang Sanzang pingsan, mencuri barangnya, dan membawanya ke Flower-Fruit Mountain untuk membentuk rombongan sendiri. Dalam novel, sosok itu memukul Tang Sanzang dan merampas dua bungkusan, lalu berkata bahwa ia sendiri akan mengambil kitab suci ke Barat.
long_description.en: According to Wikipedia's summary, he hoped to replace Sun Wukong and gain his rewards from the Buddha. He appears disguised as Sun Wukong, knocks Tang Sanzang unconscious, steals his baggage, and takes it to Flower-Fruit Mountain to set up a band of his own. In the novel, the figure strikes Tang Sanzang and seizes two bundles, then says he himself will go west to fetch the scriptures.

long_description.id: Di alam baka, Diting menyatakan bahwa kesaktian siluman itu sama dengan Sun Wukong sehingga ia tak bisa ditangkap di sana. Di hadapan Rulai, kera itu dikenali sebagai Liu'er Mihou yang serupa rupa dan suara dengan Sun Wukong; ia berubah menjadi lebah, dikurung mangkuk emas, lalu dipukul mati oleh Sun Wukong. Sang Bodhisattva kemudian memberi tahu Tang Sanzang bahwa pemukulnya adalah Sun Wukong palsu.
long_description.en: In the underworld, Diting states that the demon's powers are the same as Sun Wukong's so he cannot be captured there. Before Rulai, the monkey is identified as Liu'er Mihou, matching Sun Wukong in form and voice; he turns into a bee, is trapped under a golden bowl, and is struck dead by Sun Wukong. The Bodhisattva then tells Tang Sanzang that the one who struck him was the false Sun Wukong.

cultural_context.id: Wikipedia mencatat tafsir bahwa nama tokoh ini mungkin merujuk pada pepatah "rahasia tidak aman di antara enam telinga", dan bahwa dua kera itu mungkin metafora pikiran sejati dan pikiran palsu dalam Buddhisme Tiongkok.
cultural_context.en: Wikipedia records interpretations that the name may allude to the saying "a secret is not safe between six ears", and that the two monkeys may be metaphors for the true mind and the false mind in Chinese Buddhism.

who.id: Kera spiritual berwujud kembaran Sun Wukong dalam novel Journey to the West.
who.en: A spiritual monkey who takes the form of a double of Sun Wukong in the novel Journey to the West.

origin.id: Novel Journey to the West karya Wu Cheng'en.
origin.en: The novel Journey to the West by Wu Cheng'en.

role.id: Penyamar yang menggantikan Sun Wukong di hadapan Tang Sanzang dan merampas barangnya.
role.en: An impersonator who takes Sun Wukong's place before Tang Sanzang and seizes his baggage.

famous_for.id: Kemiripannya dengan Sun Wukong yang begitu sempurna sampai tak seorang pun dapat membedakan keduanya hingga mereka menghadap Buddha.
famous_for.en: His likeness to Sun Wukong, so perfect that no one could tell them apart until they appeared before the Buddha.

name.id: Menyamar sebagai Sun Wukong dan berubah menjadi lebah
name.en: Impersonating Sun Wukong and turning into a bee

description.id: Ia menyamar sebagai Sun Wukong dan, saat terdesak di hadapan Rulai, berubah menjadi lebah.
description.en: He impersonates Sun Wukong and, when cornered before Rulai, turns into a bee.

description.id: Menurut Rulai, ia dapat mengetahui kejadian sejauh seribu li dan ucapan manusia, serta mengetahui sebelum dan sesudah.
description.en: According to Rulai, he can know events a thousand li away and what people say, and knows before and after.

title.en: The real and the false Sun Wukong

role.id: Sun Wukong palsu yang menyaingi Sun Wukong asli sampai dikenali Buddha.
role.en: The false Sun Wukong who rivals the real one until the Buddha identifies him.

summary.id: Sosok yang menyerupai Sun Wukong memukul Tang Sanzang dan merampas bungkusannya, lalu mengaku akan mengambil kitab sendiri. Tak seorang pun dapat membedakan keduanya hingga keduanya menghadap Rulai, yang mengungkapkan jati dirinya. Sun Wukong membunuhnya setelah Rulai mengurungnya di bawah mangkuk emas.
summary.en: A figure resembling Sun Wukong strikes Tang Sanzang and seizes his bundles, then claims he will fetch the scriptures himself. No one can tell the two apart until they appear before Rulai, who reveals his identity. Sun Wukong kills him after Rulai traps him under a golden bowl.

description.id: Wikipedia mencatat bahwa Six-Eared Macaque dilahirkan kembali dalam salah satu sekuel tidak resmi paling awal dari Xiyouji, yaitu Xu Xiyouji.
description.en: Wikipedia notes that the Six-Eared Macaque is reincarnated in one of the earliest unofficial sequels to Xiyouji, Xu Xiyouji.

note.id: Kembaran, rekan, dan saingan Sun Wukong menurut Hongmei Sun; Sun Wukong akhirnya membunuhnya.
note.en: Sun Wukong's doppelganger, peer, and rival according to Hongmei Sun; Sun Wukong finally kills him.

note.id: Ia memukul Tang Sanzang dan merampas barangnya.
note.en: He strikes Tang Sanzang and seizes his baggage.

learning_questions.id: Mengapa tokoh yang menirukan Sun Wukong begitu sulit dibedakan dari aslinya dalam kisah ini?
learning_questions.en: Why is the character who imitates Sun Wukong so hard to tell apart from the original in this story?

learning_questions.id: Apa makna kisah dua kera jika dibaca sebagai metafora pikiran sejati dan pikiran palsu?
learning_questions.en: What does the story of the two monkeys mean when read as a metaphor of the true mind and the false mind?

learning_questions.id: Bagaimana penafsiran akademis berbeda dari apa yang dikatakan teks novel itu sendiri?
learning_questions.en: How do scholarly interpretations differ from what the text of the novel itself says?

claims.quote: is a major antagonist and one of the most powerful characters in Wu Cheng'en's fantasy novel Journey to the West, best remembered for closely impersonating Sun Wukong (Monkey King).

statement.id: Six-Eared Macaque adalah antagonis utama dan salah satu tokoh paling kuat dalam novel fantasi Journey to the West (Perjalanan ke Barat) karya Wu Cheng'en, yang paling diingat karena menirukan Sun Wukong (Monkey King) dengan sangat mirip.
statement.en: Six-Eared Macaque is a major antagonist and one of the most powerful characters in Wu Cheng'en's fantasy novel Journey to the West, best remembered for closely impersonating Sun Wukong (Monkey King).

claims.quote: The Six-Eared Macaque (Chinese: 六耳獼猴; pinyin: Liù'ěr míhóu)

statement.id: Nama Tionghoa Six-Eared Macaque adalah 六耳獼猴, dalam pinyin Liù'ěr míhóu.
statement.en: The Chinese name of the Six-Eared Macaque is 六耳獼猴, in pinyin Liù'ěr míhóu.

claims.quote: according to the Buddha, one of the four spiritual primates that do not belong to any of the ten categories that all beings in the universe are classified under.

statement.id: Menurut Buddha dalam novel, Six-Eared Macaque adalah satu dari empat primata spiritual yang tidak termasuk dalam sepuluh golongan yang menjadi pengelompokan semua makhluk di alam semesta.
statement.en: According to the Buddha in the novel, the Six-Eared Macaque is one of the four spiritual primates that do not belong to any of the ten categories into which all beings in the universe are classified.

claims.quote: Buddha also says that the Six-Eared Macaque is "near-omniscient" (thanks to his six ears eavesdropping upon many tidbits of information around him far and wide), "knowledgeable of past and future" and "comprehensive of all things".

statement.id: Menurut ringkasan Wikipedia, Buddha juga berkata bahwa Six-Eared Macaque "hampir mahatahu" (near-omniscient) karena enam telinganya menyadap banyak informasi di sekelilingnya, "mengetahui masa lalu dan masa depan", dan "memahami segala hal".
statement.en: According to Wikipedia's summary, the Buddha also says the Six-Eared Macaque is "near-omniscient" because his six ears eavesdrop on information around him, "knowledgeable of past and future" and "comprehensive of all things".

claims.quote: Hoping to replace Sun Wukong and gain his rewards from the Buddha in Sun Wukong's place, the Six-Eared Macaque first appears in Xiliang (西粱) in disguise as Sun Wukong. He knocks Tang Sanzang unconscious and steals the baggage and paperwork which he takes to Flower-Fruit Mountain to set up his own pilgrim band.

statement.id: Menurut ringkasan Wikipedia, dengan harapan menggantikan Sun Wukong dan menerima ganjarannya dari Buddha, Six-Eared Macaque pertama kali muncul di Xiliang (西粱) menyamar sebagai Sun Wukong. Ia membuat Tang Sanzang pingsan, mencuri barang dan dokumennya, lalu membawanya ke Flower-Fruit Mountain untuk membentuk rombongan peziarahnya sendiri.
statement.en: According to Wikipedia's summary, hoping to replace Sun Wukong and gain his rewards from the Buddha, the Six-Eared Macaque first appears in Xiliang (西粱) disguised as Sun Wukong. He knocks Tang Sanzang unconscious, steals his baggage and paperwork, and takes them to Flower-Fruit Mountain to set up his own pilgrim band.

claims.quote: The Six-Eared Macaque attempts to flee when he hears the Buddha speak about his true identity, but the Buddha traps him under a giant golden alms bowl. The macaque is then killed by Sun Wukong.

statement.id: Menurut ringkasan Wikipedia, Six-Eared Macaque mencoba kabur saat mendengar Buddha membicarakan jati dirinya, tetapi Buddha mengurungnya di bawah mangkuk sedekah emas raksasa; setelah itu ia dibunuh Sun Wukong.
statement.en: According to Wikipedia's summary, the Six-Eared Macaque tries to flee when he hears the Buddha speak of his true identity, but the Buddha traps him under a giant golden alms bowl; the macaque is then killed by Sun Wukong.

claims.quote: 那行者變了臉，發怒生嗔，喝罵長老道：「你這個狠心的潑禿！十分賤我。」掄鐵棒，丟了磁杯，望長老脊背上砑了一下。那長老昏暈在地，不能言語，被他把兩個青氈包袱提在手中，駕觔斗雲，不知去向。

statement.id: Dalam novel, sosok yang tampil sebagai Sun Wukong (行者) di Bab 57 memarahi Tang Sanzang, memukulnya dengan tongkat besi hingga pingsan, lalu membawa kabur dua bungkusan kain dengan awan salto.
statement.en: In the novel, the figure who appears as Sun Wukong (行者) in chapter 57 scolds Tang Sanzang, strikes him on the back with an iron staff until he faints, and then flies off on a somersault cloud with two bundles.

claims.quote: 我打唐僧，搶行李，不因我不上西方，亦不因我愛居此地。我今熟讀了牒文，我自己上西方拜佛求經，送上東土，我獨成功，教那南贍部洲人立我為祖，萬代傳名也。
claims.locator: Bab 57, ucapan "Sun Wukong" di Gua Tirai Air

statement.id: Dalam novel, "Sun Wukong" di Gua Tirai Air berkata bahwa ia memukul Tang Sanzang dan merampas barangnya, dan bahwa ia sendiri akan pergi ke Barat untuk menghadap Buddha dan mengambil kitab, agar dunia mengangkatnya sebagai perintis dan namanya dikenang turun-temurun.
statement.en: In the novel, the "Sun Wukong" at the Water Curtain Cave says that he beat Tang Sanzang and took his baggage, and that he himself will go west to worship the Buddha and fetch the scriptures, so that the world will honor him as a founder and his name will be passed down for generations.

claims.quote: 妖精神通，與孫大聖無二。幽冥之神，能有多少法力？故此不能擒拿。

statement.id: Dalam novel, Diting (諦聽) berkata di alam baka bahwa kesaktian siluman itu sama dengan Sun Wukong, sehingga para dewa alam baka tidak mampu menangkapnya.
statement.en: In the novel, Diting (諦聽) says in the underworld that the demon's powers are the same as Sun Wukong's, so the gods of the underworld cannot capture him.

claims.quote: 又有四猴混世，不入十類之種。」菩薩道：「敢問是那四猴？」如來道：「第一是靈明石猴，通變化，識天時，知地利，移星換斗；第二是赤尻馬猴，曉陰陽，會人事，善出入，避死延生；第三是通臂猿猴，拿日月，縮千山，辨休咎，乾坤摩弄；第四是六耳獼猴，善聆音，能察理，知前後，萬物皆明。

statement.id: Dalam novel, Rulai (如來, Buddha) menyebut empat kera yang tidak termasuk sepuluh golongan makhluk: kera batu Lingming (靈明石猴), kera pantat merah (赤尻馬猴), kera lengan panjang (通臂猿猴), dan yang keempat Liu'er Mihou (六耳獼猴), yang pandai mendengar, mampu menelaah, tahu sebelum dan sesudah, dan memahami segala hal.
statement.en: In the novel, Rulai (如來, the Buddha) names four monkeys outside the ten categories of beings: the Lingming stone monkey (靈明石猴), the red-buttocked horse monkey (赤尻馬猴), the long-armed ape (通臂猿猴), and the fourth, Liu'er Mihou (六耳獼猴), skilled at listening, able to discern reason, knowing before and after, and understanding all things.

claims.quote: 此猴若立一處，能知千里外之事；凡人說話，亦能知之。故此善聆音，能察理，知前後，萬物皆明。與真悟空同像同音者，六耳獼猴也。

statement.id: Dalam novel, Rulai (如來) berkata bahwa bila kera ini berdiri di satu tempat ia dapat mengetahui kejadian sejauh seribu li dan juga ucapan manusia, dan bahwa Liu'er Mihou (六耳獼猴) adalah yang serupa rupa dan suara dengan Sun Wukong (真悟空) yang asli.
statement.en: In the novel, Rulai (如來) says that when this monkey stands in one place he can know events a thousand li away and also what people say, and that Liu'er Mihou (六耳獼猴) is the one who matches the real Sun Wukong (真悟空) in form and voice.

claims.quote: 那獼猴毛骨悚然，料著難脫，即忙搖身一變，變作個蜜蜂兒，往上便飛。如來將金缽盂撇起去，正蓋著那蜂兒，落下來。

statement.id: Dalam novel, kera itu berubah menjadi seekor lebah (蜜蜂兒) dan terbang ke atas, tetapi Rulai (如來) melemparkan mangkuk emas (金缽盂) yang jatuh menutupi lebah itu.
statement.en: In the novel, the monkey transforms into a bee (蜜蜂兒) and flies upward, but Rulai (如來) throws his golden bowl (金缽盂), which falls and covers the bee.

claims.quote: 大眾一發上前，把缽盂揭起，果然見了本像，是一個六耳獼猴。孫大聖忍不住，掄起鐵棒，劈頭一下打死，至今絕此一種。

statement.id: Dalam novel, ketika mangkuk diangkat, tampaklah wujud aslinya, Liu'er Mihou (六耳獼猴); Sun Wukong (孫大聖) tak tahan dan memukul kepalanya dengan tongkat besi sampai mati, sehingga jenis ini punah.
statement.en: In the novel, when the bowl is lifted his true form appears, a Liu'er Mihou (六耳獼猴); Sun Wukong (孫大聖) cannot hold back and strikes his head dead with the iron staff, so that this kind is extinct.

claims.quote: 菩薩道：「唐僧，前日打你的，乃假行者六耳獼猴也。幸如來知識，已被悟空打死。

statement.id: Dalam novel, sang Bodhisattva memberi tahu Tang Sanzang bahwa yang memukulnya tempo hari adalah Sun Wukong palsu (假行者), yaitu Liu'er Mihou (六耳獼猴), yang telah dibunuh Sun Wukong berkat pengenalan Rulai.
statement.en: In the novel, the Bodhisattva tells Tang Sanzang that the one who struck him the other day was the false Sun Wukong (假行者), Liu'er Mihou (六耳獼猴), who has been killed by Sun Wukong thanks to Rulai's recognition.

short_description.id: Abumi-guchi adalah yōkai Jepang yang digambar Toriyama Sekien dalam kumpulan ilustrasi makhluk gaibnya.
short_description.en: Abumi-guchi is a Japanese yōkai illustrated by Toriyama Sekien in his collection of supernatural beings.

long_description.id: Abumi-guchi digambarkan sebagai yōkai berbulu yang namanya secara harfiah berarti “mulut sanggurdi”. Toriyama Sekien memasukkannya ke Gazu Hyakki Tsurezure Bukuro. Halaman berkas Commons mencatat ilustrasi tersebut bertanggal 1784.
long_description.en: Abumi-guchi is depicted as a furry yōkai whose name literally means “stirrup mouth.” Toriyama Sekien included it in Gazu Hyakki Tsurezure Bukuro. The Commons file page dates the illustration to 1784.

long_description.id: Dalam bahasa Jepang namanya ditulis 鐙口 dan dibaca あぶみくち. Ia digambarkan sebagai yōkai berwujud sanggurdi (abumi, salah satu perlengkapan berkuda) yang ditumbuhi mulut dan mata. Keterangan Sekien hampir tidak menjelaskan jenis yōkai ini, sehingga muncul dugaan bahwa ia adalah sanggurdi seorang panglima yang gugur dan dibiarkan terbuang di padang.
long_description.en: In Japanese the name is written 鐙口 and read あぶみくち. It is depicted as a yōkai in the form of a stirrup (abumi, a piece of horse tack) with a mouth and eyes. Sekien's caption hardly explains what kind of yōkai it is, so it has been suggested that it is the stirrup of a military commander killed in battle and left abandoned in the field.

long_description.id: Sekien menggambar Abumi-guchi pada halaman bentang yang sama dengan Kurayarō (鞍野郎). Keduanya juga diduga diciptakan dengan motif Tsurezuregusa, yang pada bagian ke-186 memuat peringatan tentang perlengkapan berkuda seperti pelana. Mizuki Shigeru menjelaskan bahwa Abumi-guchi menanti tuan yang tak akan kembali seperti anjing menanti pemiliknya, tetapi Hyakki Tsurezure Bukuro sendiri tidak memuat tradisi demikian.
long_description.en: Sekien drew Abumi-guchi on the same double-page spread as Kurayarō (鞍野郎). The two are also thought to have been created on the motif of Tsurezuregusa, which in section 186 contains a caution about horse tack such as saddles. Mizuki Shigeru explains that Abumi-guchi waits for a master who will not return, like a dog waiting for its owner, but Hyakki Tsurezure Bukuro itself does not state such a tradition.

short_description.id: Âu Cơ adalah dewi atau peri gunung dalam mitos asal-usul bangsa Vietnam, yang menikah dengan Lạc Long Quân dan melahirkan seratus anak, leluhur orang Vietnam.
short_description.en: Âu Cơ is a mountain goddess or fairy in the Vietnamese origin myth who married Lạc Long Quân and bore a hundred children, ancestors of the Vietnamese people.

long_description.id: Menurut mitos penciptaan bangsa Vietnam, Âu Cơ adalah dewi salju pegunungan yang abadi. Ia menikah dengan Lạc Long Quân, raja naga, dan melahirkan kantong telur yang menetaskan seratus anak, yang dikenal bersama sebagai Bách Việt dan menjadi leluhur bangsa Vietnam. Karena itu ia sering dihormati sebagai ibu peradaban Vietnam.
long_description.en: According to the Vietnamese creation myth, Âu Cơ was an immortal mountain snow goddess. She married Lạc Long Quân, the dragon lord, and bore an egg sac that hatched a hundred children, known together as Bách Việt, ancestors of the Vietnamese people. She is therefore often honoured as the mother of Vietnamese civilization.

long_description.id: Dalam kisahnya, Âu Cơ adalah tiên (makhluk abadi) cantik yang tinggal di pegunungan bersalju dan berkelana menolong orang sakit karena mahir dalam pengobatan. Suatu hari ia bertemu monster dan berubah menjadi burung bangau untuk melarikan diri; Lạc Long Quân membunuh monster itu dengan batu, dan Âu Cơ pun jatuh cinta kepadanya.
long_description.en: In her story, Âu Cơ was a beautiful tiên (immortal) living in the snowy mountains who travelled to help the sick because she was skilled in medicine. One day she met a monster and turned into a crane to escape; Lạc Long Quân killed the monster with a rock, and Âu Cơ fell in love with him.

long_description.id: Meski saling mencintai, Âu Cơ merindukan pegunungan dan Lạc Long Quân merindukan laut. Mereka berpisah dan masing-masing membawa lima puluh anak; Âu Cơ menetap di pegunungan dan membesarkan para pemimpin yang kemudian dikenal sebagai raja-raja Hùng. Dalam versi lain, Lạc Long Quân berkata bahwa ia bersifat seperti naga di air dan Âu Cơ seperti peri di gunung, sehingga mereka harus hidup terpisah, tetapi saling menolong bila salah satu kelompok tertimpa kemalangan.
long_description.en: Though they loved each other, Âu Cơ longed for the mountains and Lạc Long Quân for the sea. They parted, each taking fifty children; Âu Cơ settled in the mountains and raised the leaders later known as the Hùng kings. In another telling, Lạc Long Quân said he was by nature like a dragon in the water and she like a fairy in the mountain, so they must live apart, yet help each other if either group met misfortune.

long_description.id: Legenda ini tercatat dalam Lĩnh Nam chích quái (abad ke-14) dan Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư (abad ke-15), dengan perbedaan: dalam Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư Âu Cơ adalah putri Đế Lai, sedangkan dalam Lĩnh Nam chích quái ia selir Đế Lai sebelum menikah dengan Lạc Long Quân. Kisah Âu Cơ dan Lạc Long Quân diajarkan luas di sekolah-sekolah Vietnam, dan karena legenda ini orang Vietnam menyebut diri keturunan naga dan peri. Ngô Sĩ Liên mengomentari dalam sử ký bahwa hubungan kedua leluhur itu agak primitif, karena ayah Lạc, Kinh Dương Vương, dan kakek Âu, Đế Nghi, bersaudara.
long_description.en: The legend is recorded in the Lĩnh Nam chích quái (14th century) and the Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư (15th century), with differences: in the Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư Âu Cơ is Đế Lai's daughter, while in the Lĩnh Nam chích quái she was Đế Lai's concubine before marrying Lạc Long Quân. The story of Âu Cơ and Lạc Long Quân is widely taught in Vietnamese schools, and because of it the Vietnamese call themselves descendants of the dragon and the fairy. Ngô Sĩ Liên commented in the sử ký that the relationship between the two progenitors was somewhat primitive, because Kinh Dương Vương, father of Lạc, and Đế Nghi, grandfather of Âu, were brothers.

cultural_context.en: Because of this legend, the Vietnamese refer to themselves as descendants of the Dragon and the Fairy, from one family long ago.

statement.id: Menurut mitos penciptaan bangsa Vietnam, Âu Cơ (甌姬) adalah dewi salju pegunungan yang abadi, menikah dengan Lạc Long Quân, dan melahirkan kantong telur yang menetaskan seratus anak (Bách Việt), leluhur bangsa Vietnam; ia sering dihormati sebagai ibu peradaban Vietnam.
statement.en: According to the Vietnamese creation myth, Âu Cơ (甌姬) was an immortal mountain snow goddess who married Lạc Long Quân and bore an egg sac hatching a hundred children (Bách Việt), ancestors of the Vietnamese; she is honoured as mother of Vietnamese civilization.

claims.quote: Âu Cơ was a beautiful tiên (immortal) who lived high in the snow-capped mountains. She traveled to help those who suffered from illnesses since she was very skillful in medicine and had a sympathetic heart.

statement.id: Âu Cơ adalah tiên (makhluk abadi) cantik yang tinggal di pegunungan bersalju dan berkelana menolong orang sakit karena mahir pengobatan dan berhati welas asih.
statement.en: Âu Cơ was a beautiful tiên (immortal) in the snowy mountains who travelled to help the sick, being skilled in medicine and compassionate.

claims.quote: It frightened her, so she transformed into a crane to fly away. Lạc Long Quân, the dragon king from the sea, passed by and saw the crane in danger. He grabbed a nearby rock and killed the monster with it.

statement.en: Frightened, Âu Cơ turned into a crane to fly away; Lạc Long Quân, the dragon king from the sea, saw and killed the monster with a rock.

claims.quote: They separated, each taking 50 children. Âu Cơ settled in the Vietnamese snow-covered mountains where she raised fifty young, intelligent, strong leaders, later known as the Hùng Vương, Hùng kings.

statement.id: Mereka berpisah dengan masing-masing membawa 50 anak; Âu Cơ menetap di pegunungan bersalju dan membesarkan lima puluh pemimpin yang kemudian dikenal sebagai raja-raja Hùng (Hùng Vương).
statement.en: They separated, each taking 50 children; Âu Cơ settled in the snowy mountains and raised fifty leaders later known as the Hùng kings (Hùng Vương).

short_description.id: Baigujing (Siluman Tulang Putih) adalah iblis perempuan pengubah wujud dalam novel Journey to the West. Wujud aslinya kerangka; ia menyamar tiga kali untuk memakan daging Tang Sanzang tetapi dikenali Sun Wukong.
short_description.en: Baigujing (White Bone Spirit) is a shapeshifting demoness in the novel Journey to the West. Her true form is a skeleton; she disguises herself three times to eat the flesh of Tang Sanzang but is recognized by Sun Wukong.

long_description.id: Baigujing adalah tokoh sastra dari novel abad ke-16 Journey to the West (Perjalanan ke Barat), yang oleh Wikipedia disebut iblis perempuan pengubah wujud dengan wujud asli berupa kerangka. Terjemahan William John Francis Jenner menamainya White Bone Spirit. Dalam novel, Sun Wukong menyebutnya jiangshi yang menjelma pengacau, dan di punggungnya tertulis nama Baigu Furen.
long_description.en: Baigujing is a literary character from the 16th-century novel Journey to the West, called by Wikipedia a shapeshifting demoness whose true form is a skeleton. The William John Francis Jenner translation names her White Bone Spirit. In the novel, Sun Wukong calls her a jiangshi that has turned into a troublemaker, and her back bears the name Baigu Furen.

long_description.id: Dalam novel, ia mengetahui bahwa memakan sepotong daging Tang Sanzang memberi umur panjang. Ia lalu menyamar sebagai gadis cantik dengan kendi dan botol, kemudian sebagai perempuan tua dan seorang kakek. Isi kendi ternyata belatung, katak, dan kodok. Sun Wukong, dengan mata api bermata emasnya, mengenali penyamaran itu; ia memakai jieshi fa untuk meninggalkan mayat palsu ketika dipukul.
long_description.en: In the novel, she learns that eating a piece of the flesh of Tang Sanzang grants long life. She disguises herself as a beautiful girl with a jar and bottle, then as an old woman and an old man. The contents of the jar turn out to be maggots, frogs, and toads. Sun Wukong, with his fiery golden eyes, recognizes the disguise; she uses the jieshi fa technique to leave a false corpse when struck.

long_description.id: Pada akhirnya Sun Wukong memukul mati sosok itu dan tubuhnya menjadi setumpuk tengkorak. Zhu Bajie menghasut Tang Sanzang agar tidak percaya bahwa itu siluman, dan Tang Sanzang kembali merapal mantra; akhirnya Sun Wukong berpamitan dan kembali ke Gua Tirai Air.
long_description.en: In the end Sun Wukong strikes the figure dead and its body becomes a pile of skeleton. Zhu Bajie goads Tang Sanzang into doubting that it was a demon, and Tang Sanzang chants the spell again; in the end Sun Wukong takes his leave and returns to the Water Curtain Cave.

statement.en: In the novel, the demon is delighted because for years she has heard that Tang Sanzang (唐和尚) is the incarnation of Jinchanzi (金蟬子) and that anyone who eats a piece of his flesh will live a long life.

statement.id: Dalam novel, siluman itu berubah (搖身一變) menjadi gadis cantik yang membawa kendi hijau dan botol porselen hijau, lalu berjalan langsung menuju Tang Sanzang (唐僧).
statement.en: In the novel, the demon transforms (搖身一變) into a beautiful girl carrying a green clay jar and a green porcelain bottle, and walks straight toward Tang Sanzang (唐僧).

claims.quote: 沙僧攙著長老，近前看時，那裡是甚香米飯，卻是一罐子拖尾巴的長蛆；也不是麵觔，卻是幾個青蛙、癩蝦蟆，滿地亂跳。

statement.id: Dalam novel, ketika isi kendi dan botol itu diperiksa, nasi harum ternyata berupa belatung berekor dan "gluten goreng" berupa katak dan kodok yang melompat ke mana-mana.
statement.en: In the novel, when the jar and bottle are checked, the fragrant rice turns out to be a jar of long tailed maggots and the fried gluten turns out to be frogs and toads hopping everywhere.

claims.quote: 那怪物有些手段，使個「解屍法」，見行者棍子來時，他卻抖擻精神，預先走了，把一個假屍首打死在地下。

statement.id: Dalam novel, siluman itu memakai "jieshi fa" (解屍法) saat tongkat Sun Wukong datang: ia meloloskan diri lebih dulu dan meninggalkan mayat palsu yang terpukul mati.
statement.en: In the novel, the demon uses the "jieshi fa" (解屍法) technique when Sun Wukong's staff comes: she slips away beforehand and leaves a false corpse struck dead on the ground.

claims.quote: 好妖精，按落陰雲，在那前山坡下搖身一變，變作個老婦人，年滿八旬，手拄著一根彎頭竹杖，一步一聲的哭著走來。 ... 好妖精，按聳陰風，在山坡下搖身一變，變做一個老公公

statement.id: Dalam novel, siluman itu kemudian berubah menjadi perempuan tua berusia delapan puluh tahun yang berjalan sambil menangis, lalu menjadi seorang kakek.
statement.en: In the novel, the demon later transforms into an old woman of eighty who walks along weeping, and then into an old man.

claims.quote: 只見那行者自南山頂上摘了幾個桃子，托著缽盂，一觔斗，點將回來，睜火眼金睛觀看，認得那女子是個妖精，放下缽盂，掣鐵棒，當頭就打。

statement.id: Dalam novel, Sun Wukong kembali dari memetik buah persik, menatap dengan mata api bermata emas (火眼金睛), mengenali gadis itu sebagai siluman, dan langsung memukulnya dengan tongkat besi.
statement.en: In the novel, Sun Wukong returns from picking peaches, looks with his fiery golden eyes (火眼金睛), recognizes the girl as a demon, and strikes at her at once with his iron staff.

claims.quote: 他是個潛靈作怪的僵尸，在此迷人敗本，被我打殺，他就現了本相。他那脊梁上有一行字，叫做『白骨夫人』。

statement.id: Dalam novel, Sun Wukong berkata bahwa makhluk itu adalah jiangshi (僵尸, mayat) yang menjelma menjadi pengacau; setelah dibunuh ia menampakkan wujud aslinya, dan di punggungnya tertulis "Baigu Furen" (白骨夫人).
statement.en: In the novel, Sun Wukong says the creature is a jiangshi (僵尸, corpse) that has become a troublemaker; once killed it shows its true form, and on its back is written "Baigu Furen" (白骨夫人).

claims.quote: 卻是一堆粉骷髏在那裡。唐僧大驚道：「悟空，這個人才死了，怎麼就化作一堆骷髏？」

statement.id: Dalam novel, tubuh yang baru mati itu ternyata berupa setumpuk tengkorak putih (粉骷髏), dan Tang Sanzang terkejut karenanya.
statement.en: In the novel, the body that has just died turns out to be a pile of white skeleton (粉骷髏), and Tang Sanzang is shocked.

claims.quote: 怎禁那八戒傍邊唆嘴道：「師父，他的手重棍兇，把人打死，只怕你念那話兒，故意變化這個模樣，掩你的眼目哩。」唐僧果然耳軟，又信了他，隨復念起。

statement.id: Dalam novel, Zhu Bajie (八戒) menghasut Tang Sanzang dengan mengatakan bahwa Sun Wukong sengaja mengubah mayat itu menjadi kerangka untuk mengelabui mata gurunya; Tang Sanzang percaya dan kembali merapal mantra.
statement.en: In the novel, Zhu Bajie (八戒) goads Tang Sanzang by saying Sun Wukong deliberately changed the corpse into a skeleton to fool his master; Tang Sanzang believes him and chants the spell again.

claims.quote: 師父，此山叫做蛇回獸怕的白虎嶺，正西下面是我家。我父母在堂，看經好善，廣齋方上遠近僧人。

statement.id: Dalam novel, sosok gadis yang menyamar itu menyebut bahwa gunung itu bernama Baihu Ling (白虎嶺), tempat ular mundur dan hewan buas takut.
statement.en: In the novel, the disguised girl says the mountain is called Baihu Ling (白虎嶺), where snakes turn back and beasts take fright.

claims.quote: 你看他忍氣別了師父，縱觔斗雲，徑回花果山水簾洞去了。獨自個悽悽慘慘，忽聞得水聲聒耳。

statement.id: Dalam novel, setelah diusir, Sun Wukong berpamitan dengan menahan amarah dan terbang dengan awan salto kembali ke Gua Tirai Air (水簾洞) di Gunung Buah Bunga (花果山).
statement.en: In the novel, after being dismissed, Sun Wukong takes leave of his master holding back his anger and flies on a somersault cloud back to the Water Curtain Cave (水簾洞) on Flower-Fruit Mountain (花果山).

claims.quote: 卻說常言有云：「山高必有怪，嶺峻卻生精。」果然這山上有一個妖精，孫大聖去時，驚動那怪。

statement.id: Dalam novel, dikatakan bahwa ada pepatah "gunung tinggi pasti ada siluman, bukit curam melahirkan roh", dan memang ada seorang yaojing (妖精, siluman) di gunung itu.
statement.en: In the novel, a saying is cited, "where mountains are high there must be monsters, where ridges are steep spirits are born," and indeed there is a yaojing (妖精, demon) on that mountain.

claims.quote: In The Monkey King Conquers the Demon, Baigujing is the main antagonist.

statement.id: Dalam film The Monkey King Conquers the Demon, Baigujing adalah antagonis utama.
statement.en: In The Monkey King Conquers the Demon, Baigujing is the main antagonist.

claims.quote: In the TV series Lego Monkie Kid, Baigujing (referred to as Lady Bone Demon) is the main antagonist in the second and third season.

statement.id: Dalam serial TV Lego Monkie Kid, Baigujing (disebut Lady Bone Demon) adalah antagonis utama di musim kedua dan ketiga.
statement.en: In the TV series Lego Monkie Kid, Baigujing (referred to as Lady Bone Demon) is the main antagonist in the second and third seasons.

claims.quote: Provoked, Sun finally beats Baigujing with his staff and kills the demon, revealing that it was just a skeleton spirit.

statement.id: Menurut ringkasan Wikipedia, Sun Wukong akhirnya memukul Baigujing dengan tongkatnya dan membunuhnya, sehingga tampak bahwa makhluk itu hanyalah roh kerangka (skeleton spirit).
statement.en: According to Wikipedia's summary, Sun Wukong finally beats Baigujing with his staff and kills her, revealing that she was just a skeleton spirit.

Terjemahan Inggris domain publik (Timothy Richard 1913, Helen Hayes 1930) hanya ada di archive.org sehingga tidak bisa diperiksa otomatis; Gutenberg #23962 (teks Mandarin) berisi pemenggalan baris sehingga kutipannya tidak bisa dicocokkan. Wikipedia en tidak menyebut tahun film dan serial dalam kalimat yang dikutip, jadi tahun tidak diisi.
