short_description.id: Suvannamaccha adalah putri duyung emas dalam Ramayana versi Asia Tenggara, putri Rahwana yang semula menghalangi Hanoman membangun jembatan ke Lanka lalu jatuh cinta kepadanya.
short_description.en: Suvannamaccha is the golden mermaid of Southeast Asian versions of the Ramayana, a daughter of Ravana who first hinders Hanuman's bridge to Lanka and then falls in love with him.

long_description.id: Suvannamaccha, yang namanya berarti ikan emas, adalah putri Rahwana (Thotsakan) dalam Ramayana versi Thailand dan Asia Tenggara lainnya. Ia putri duyung yang mencoba menggagalkan rencana Hanoman membangun jembatan ke Lanka, tetapi justru jatuh cinta kepadanya. Kisahnya menonjol dalam Reamker, epos Kamboja, dan Ramakien, epos nasional Thailand, tetapi tidak ada dalam Ramayana karya Walmiki.
long_description.en: Suvannamaccha, whose name means golden fish, is a daughter of Ravana (Thotsakan) in Thai and other Southeast Asian versions of the Ramayana. This mermaid sets out to wreck Hanuman's plan for a causeway to Lanka, only to fall for him. Her story is prominent in the Reamker, Cambodia's epic, and the Ramakien, Thailand's national epic, but it is absent from Valmiki's Ramayana.

long_description.id: Dalam kisahnya, batu-batu yang dilemparkan pasukan kera ke laut untuk membangun jembatan selalu hilang keesokan harinya. Hanoman menyelam dan menemukan sekawanan putri duyung yang mengangkut batu-batu itu di bawah pimpinan Suvannamaccha. Ia berulang kali menyerang tetapi tak berhasil, lalu mengganti taktik dan merayunya hingga keduanya bersatu di dasar laut. Dalam salah satu penuturan, Hanoman diperintah menyeberangkan pasukan ke Lanka untuk membantu Rama menyelamatkan Sita dari Rahwana; setelah serangannya gagal, ia meninggalkan cara kasar dan mencurahkan kelembutan hingga Suvannamaccha membalas cintanya dan mereka berbahagia di bawah air. Putra mereka, Macchanu, kemudian melawan Hanoman dalam pertempuran melawan pasukan Rahwana.
long_description.en: In her story, the rocks the monkey army threw into the sea for the bridge vanished each following day. Hanuman dived and found a band of mermaids carrying them off, led by Suvannamaccha. His repeated attacks failed, so he changed tactics and wooed her until the two were together at the bottom of the sea. In one telling, Hanuman and his army set out to build a bridge to Lanka to help Rama rescue Sita from Ravana; when his attacks fail he abandons force and showers her with tenderness until Suvannamaccha returns his love and they are happy underwater. Their son Macchanu later opposes Hanuman in a battle with Ravana's army.

long_description.id: Suvannamaccha mengaku bertindak atas perintah ayahnya. Setelah Hanoman menjelaskan alasan pembangunan jembatan, ia berhenti menghalangi dan memerintahkan para putri duyung mengembalikan batu-batu yang dicuri. Dari hubungan mereka lahir Macchanu, putra berbadan kera dan berekor ikan.
long_description.en: Suvannamaccha said she was acting on her father's orders. Once Hanuman explained why the bridge was being built, she stopped hindering it and had her mermaids return the stolen rocks. From their union came Macchanu, a son with a monkey's torso and a fish's lower body.

long_description.id: Sosok Suvannamaccha populer dalam cerita rakyat Thailand dan digambarkan pada panji kain kecil atau gambar berbingkai yang digantung sebagai jimat pembawa keberuntungan di toko dan rumah di seluruh Thailand. Kisahnya juga dipentaskan sebagai Robam Sovann Maccha, tari tradisional Kamboja.
long_description.en: Suvannamaccha is popular in Thai folklore and appears on small cloth streamers or framed pictures hung as luck-bringing charms in shops and homes across Thailand. Her story is also performed as Robam Sovann Maccha, a traditional Cambodian dance.

long_description.id: Kisah ini digambarkan dalam banyak karya: sejumlah mural, lukisan sutra Thai, ilustrasi, karya seni kertas sepia, patung, serta jimat kertas dan kain memperlihatkan putri Rahwana berpelukan dengan Hanoman. Sebuah slide wayang Thai mengutip bait lakon Ramakien tentang pengejaran sang putri duyung, dan menyebut Hanoman akhirnya menjadikannya salah satu dari banyak kekasihnya. Di Kamboja, kisahnya dibawakan sebagai tarian duet Sovann Machha; menurut sebuah artikel, tarian itu bertarikh abad ke-7, dipentaskan sebagai ritual kuil pada masa Angkor, dan kini menjadi karya terkenal Balet Kerajaan Kamboja; tarian itu juga ditampilkan oleh tujuh penari Kelompok Tari Klasik Kamboja bersama tiga tarian lain.
long_description.en: The tale is shown in many works: murals, Thai silk paintings, illustrations, sepia paper art, sculptures, and paper and cloth charms show Ravana's daughter in an embrace with Hanuman. A Thai puppet slide quotes a verse of the Ramakien play about the chase of the mermaid and says Hanuman eventually had her as one of his many mistresses. In Cambodia the story is performed as the duo dance Sovann Machha; according to one article the dance is dated to the seventh century, was performed as a temple ritual in the Angkor period, and is now a famous piece of the Royal Ballet of Cambodia; it was also performed by seven dancers of Cambodia's Classical Dance Group alongside three other dances.

did_you_know.id: Dalam Ramayana Walmiki, Hanoman tetap selibat dan putranya, Makaradhwaja, lahir dari keringatnya; kisah Suvannamaccha dan Macchanu hanya ada dalam versi Asia Tenggara.
did_you_know.en: In Valmiki's Ramayana, Hanuman stays celibate and his son Makaradhwaja is born from his sweat; the tale of Suvannamaccha and Macchanu belongs to Southeast Asian versions.

summary.id: Atas perintah Rahwana, Suvannamaccha dan para putri duyung mencuri batu jembatan Hanoman. Hanoman jatuh cinta kepadanya, menjelaskan tujuan jembatan, dan Suvannamaccha pun mengembalikan batu-batu itu. Kelak ia melahirkan putra mereka, Macchanu.
summary.en: On Ravana's orders, Suvannamaccha and her mermaids stole the stones of Hanuman's bridge. Hanuman fell in love with her and explained the bridge's purpose, and she returned the stones. She later bore their son, Macchanu.

claims.quote: Several murals, Thai silk paintings, illustrations, sepia paper art, sculptures and even paper and cloth charms depict the mermaid daughter of Ravana ... entangled in amorous embraces with Hanuman.

statement.id: Sejumlah mural, lukisan sutra Thai, ilustrasi, karya seni kertas sepia, patung, bahkan jimat kertas dan kain menggambarkan putri duyung putri Rahwana berpelukan mesra dengan Hanoman.
statement.en: Several murals, Thai silk paintings, illustrations, sepia paper art, sculptures and even paper and cloth charms depict Ravana's mermaid daughter in amorous embraces with Hanuman.

claims.quote: is also performed as Robam Sovann Maccha ... Dated to the seventh century, it was performed as a temple ritual during the Angkor period and is a famous piece in the repertoire of the Royal Ballet of Cambodia today.

statement.id: Menurut artikel ini, Robam Sovann Maccha bertarikh abad ke-7 (tertulis 'the seventh century'), dipentaskan sebagai ritual kuil pada masa Angkor, dan kini menjadi karya terkenal dalam repertoar Balet Kerajaan Kamboja.
statement.en: According to the article, Robam Sovann Maccha is dated to the seventh century, was performed as a temple ritual during the Angkor period, and is a famous piece in the repertoire of the Royal Ballet of Cambodia today.

claims.quote: Hanuman, the valiant monkey god in Hinduism, and his vanara army of anthropomorphic monkeys embark on the monumental task of building a bridge to Lanka to help Rama rescue his wife, Sita, from the clutches of Ravana.

statement.id: Hanoman, dewa kera perkasa dalam agama Hindu, bersama pasukan vanara memulai tugas besar membangun jembatan ke Lanka untuk membantu Rama menyelamatkan istrinya, Sita, dari cengkeraman Rahwana.
statement.en: Hanuman, the valiant monkey god in Hinduism, and his vanara army set out on the monumental task of building a bridge to Lanka to help Rama rescue his wife Sita from Ravana's clutches.

claims.quote: He abandons his forceful approach and showers her with tenderness instead of attacks until she, too, returns his love, and they spend a blissful period underwater.

statement.id: Hanoman meninggalkan cara kasarnya dan mencurahkan kelembutan alih-alih serangan sampai ia pun membalas cintanya, dan mereka menghabiskan masa bahagia di bawah air.
statement.en: Hanuman abandons his forceful approach and showers her with tenderness instead of attacks until she returns his love, and they spend a blissful period underwater.

claims.quote: With a vanara’s torso and the lower body of a fish, Macchanu opposes Hanumanu later during a battle with Ravana’s army.

statement.id: Macchanu, yang bertubuh atas vanara dan bertubuh bawah ikan, kemudian melawan Hanoman dalam pertempuran melawan pasukan Rahwana.
statement.en: Macchanu, with a vanara's torso and a fish's lower body, later opposes Hanuman during a battle with Ravana's army.

claims.quote: In this slide, he was trying to arrest Nang Suwan Matcha, a murmaid, to ask for information while he was on one of the duties assigned by Pra Rama. He eventually had her as one of his many mistresses.

statement.id: Menurut keterangan slide ini, Hanoman berusaha menangkap Nang Suwan Matcha, seorang 'murmaid' (putri duyung), untuk menanyakan informasi saat menjalankan salah satu tugas dari Pra Rama; ia akhirnya menjadikannya salah satu dari banyak kekasihnya.
statement.en: According to this slide's caption, Hanuman was trying to arrest Nang Suwan Matcha, a 'murmaid', to ask for information on one of the duties assigned by Pra Rama, and he eventually had her as one of his many mistresses.

text.id: Pemujaannya tercatat lazim di daerah-daerah pada awal periode Rattanakosin, dan kini berlanjut sebagai kepercayaan masa kini.
text.en: Her worship is described as commonly seen locally in the early Rattanakosin period, and it continues as a present-day belief.

cultural_context.id: Kepercayaan pada Nang Ta-khian membantu melindungi pohon tua: biksu melilitkan kain satin pada pohon-pohon itu, dan penebangan harus didahului upacara meminta izin. Para peneliti juga menggambarkan pemujaan Chao Mae Ta-khian di komunitas lokal sebagai perpaduan modernitas dan kepercayaan gaib, dengan persembahan pakaian tradisional Thai sebagai pemenuhan nazar.
cultural_context.en: Belief in Nang Ta-khian helps protect old trees: monks wrap them in satin, and felling requires a ceremony asking permission. Researchers also describe worship of Chao Mae Ta-khian in local communities as a blend of modernity and spirit belief, with traditional Thai dress offered to fulfil vows.

summary.id: Tiang ta-khian dari sungai dipercaya tempat bersemayam Nang Ta-khian. Ketika tidak dipilih menjadi tiang utama istana raja pada masa Rattanakosin, ia bersedih, menangis, dan hanyut melawan arus kembali ke sungai; dari kisah ini nama distrik Sao Hai di Saraburi berasal.
summary.en: A ta-khian pillar from the river was believed to house Nang Ta-khian. When it was not chosen as the main pillar of a king's palace in the Rattanakosin period, she grieved, wept and drifted upstream back to the river; the name of Sao Hai District in Saraburi derives from the tale.

short_description.id: Nang Ta-khian adalah roh perempuan dalam cerita rakyat Thailand yang menghuni pohon ta-khian (Hopea odorata), kadang tampil sebagai perempuan muda cantik berbusana tradisional merah atau cokelat.
short_description.en: Nang Ta-khian is a female spirit of Thai folklore who inhabits ta-khian trees (Hopea odorata), sometimes appearing as a beautiful young woman in red or brown traditional dress.

long_description.id: Nang Ta-khian, yang berarti Nona dari Ta-khian, adalah roh perempuan dalam cerita rakyat Thailand yang menghuni pohon Hopea odorata, pohon sangat besar yang dalam bahasa Thai disebut ta-khian. Ia termasuk golongan roh atau peri pohon yang disebut nang mai. Menurut tradisi lisan, ia kadang tampil sebagai perempuan muda cantik berbusana tradisional Thai berwarna kemerahan atau kecokelatan, berbeda dengan Nang Tani yang berbusana hijau.
long_description.en: Nang Ta-khian, meaning Lady of Ta-khian, is a female spirit of Thai folklore who inhabits the Hopea odorata, a very large tree called ta-khian in Thai. She belongs to the tree spirits or fairies called nang mai. In oral tradition she sometimes appears as a beautiful young woman in reddish or brownish traditional Thai dress, unlike Nang Tani, who wears green.

long_description.id: Nang Ta-khian umumnya roh hutan, karena pohon ta-khian tumbuh di hutan jauh dari permukiman. Ia menghantui sekitar pohonnya dan juga rumah yang balok, tiang, atau pilarnya dibuat dari kayu ta-khian. Ia dapat mencelakai orang jahat yang mendekati tempat tinggalnya, tetapi orang baik tidak perlu takut. Orang yang tidak menghormatinya dipercaya jatuh sakit tanpa sebab, dan baru pulih setelah memohon maaf dengan sesajen. Pohonnya hampir tidak pernah ditebang, karena rohnya akan murka dan mengikuti kayunya.
long_description.en: Nang Ta-khian is generally a forest spirit, as the ta-khian grows in forests far from settlements. She haunts the surroundings of her tree and also houses whose beams, stilts or pillars are made of ta-khian wood. She may hurt wicked people who come near her abode, but righteous people have nothing to fear. A person who disrespects her is believed to fall ill for no known reason and to recover only after apologising with offerings. The tree is almost never felled, for the spirit would be furious and follow the wood.

long_description.id: Pohon yang dihuni Nang Ta-khian biasanya dililit kain satin berwarna, dan para biksu melilitkan kain itu pada pohon tua untuk melindunginya dari penebangan. Di sebagian Thailand ia menjadi dewi pohon yang populer; kayu atau lunas perahu yang diyakini dihuninya menjadi tempat ziarah, dan kini ia sering dipuja agar beruntung dalam lotre. Kuil besar untuknya antara lain ada di Distrik Sao Hai, Saraburi, dan Amphawa, Samut Songkhram. Sebagian pohon yang sangat tua kini tetap ditebang untuk diambil kayunya, meskipun konon berbahaya menebangnya tanpa persetujuan roh penghuninya. Sebuah penelitian di sepanjang tepi Sungai Chao Phraya mencatat 164 pohon Hopea odorata besar, dan 81 di antaranya dianggap pohon keramat.
long_description.en: Trees inhabited by Nang Ta-khian are usually wrapped in coloured satin, and monks wrap old trees to protect them from logging. In parts of Thailand she has become a popular tree deity; logs or boat keels believed to house her are objects of pilgrimage, and today she is often propitiated for luck in the lottery. Larger shrines to her stand in Sao Hai District, Saraburi, and Amphawa, Samut Songkhram. Some very ancient trees are nonetheless felled today for their wood, even though cutting one without the consent of the inhabiting spirit is said to be dangerous. A study along the Chaophraya River counted 164 big Hopea odorata trees, 81 of them regarded as spiritual trees.

long_description.id: Sebuah artikel jurnal menggambarkan peralihan Nang Ta-khian dari peri pohon menjadi chao mae (dewi) yang dipuja, termasuk kisah ia muncul dalam mimpi dan meminta batang kayunya diangkat dari air. Pemujaannya sudah lazim di daerah pada awal periode Rattanakosin, dan peri pohon ta-khian juga muncul dalam puisi perjalanan (nirat). Kini ia diwujudkan secara budaya sebagai perempuan cantik, dan orang yang doanya terkabul memberikan persembahan, terutama pakaian tradisional Thai.
long_description.en: A journal article describes Nang Ta-khian's shift from tree nymph to a worshipped chao mae (goddess), including accounts of her appearing in dreams and asking for her log to be raised from the water. Her worship was already common locally in the early Rattanakosin period, and ta-khian tree nymphs also appear in travel poems (nirat). Today she is culturally embodied as a beautiful woman, and people whose prayers are answered give offerings, mostly traditional Thai dress.

claims.quote: Nang Ta-khian (Thai: นางตะเคียน, "Lady of Ta-khian") is a female spirit of the folklore of Thailand. It manifests itself as a woman that haunts Hopea odorata trees. These are very large trees known as Ta-khian (ตะเคียน) in Thai, hence her name.

statement.id: Nang Ta-khian (นางตะเคียน, 'Nona dari Ta-khian') adalah roh perempuan cerita rakyat Thailand yang tampil sebagai perempuan penghuni pohon Hopea odorata, pohon sangat besar yang disebut ta-khian.
statement.en: Nang Ta-khian (นางตะเคียน, 'Lady of Ta-khian') is a female spirit of Thai folklore appearing as a woman haunting Hopea odorata trees, very large trees called ta-khian.

claims.quote: Legends in the Thai oral tradition say the spirit inhabits a Ta-khian tree and sometimes appears as a beautiful young woman wearing traditional Thai attire, usually in reddish or brownish colours, contrasting with Nang Tani who is mostly represented in a green dress.

statement.id: Nang Ta-khian termasuk roh pohon nang mai; menurut tradisi lisan ia menghuni pohon ta-khian dan kadang tampil sebagai perempuan muda cantik berbusana Thai kemerahan atau kecokelatan, berbeda dengan Nang Tani yang berbusana hijau.
statement.en: Nang Ta-khian is a nang mai tree spirit; oral tradition says she inhabits a ta-khian tree and sometimes appears as a beautiful young woman in reddish or brownish Thai dress, unlike the green-clad Nang Tani.

claims.quote: Like all Nang Mai, Nang Ta-khian haunts the immediate environment of her tree and she may also haunt a house having beams, stilts or pillars made from Ta-khian wood. She may hurt wicked or immoral people that come close to her abode, but righteous persons have nothing to fear from her.

statement.id: Nang Ta-khian, roh hutan, menghantui sekitar pohonnya dan rumah berbalok, bertiang, atau berpilar kayu ta-khian; ia dapat mencelakai orang jahat yang mendekat, tetapi orang baik tak perlu takut.
statement.en: Nang Ta-khian, a forest spirit, haunts her tree's surroundings and houses with ta-khian beams, stilts or pillars; she may hurt the wicked who approach, but the righteous need not fear.

claims.quote: The tree is almost never felled for lumber, since the spirit will be furious and follow the wood. About the only place Ta-khian is used as lumber is in a Buddhist monastery, where the merit of the monks is considered sufficient to render the spirit harmless.

statement.id: Pohon ta-khian hampir tak pernah ditebang karena rohnya akan murka dan mengikuti kayunya; kayunya hampir hanya dipakai di biara Buddha, tempat pahala para biksu dianggap cukup untuk menjinakkannya.
statement.en: The ta-khian is almost never felled, for the spirit would be furious and follow the wood; it is used almost only in Buddhist monasteries, where monks' merit renders the spirit harmless.

claims.quote: Traditionally trees where Ta-khian resides have lengths of colored satin cloth wrapped around their trunk. In order to protect venerable old trees from logging, Buddhist monks use to wrap lengths of satin around them

statement.id: Pohon tempat Ta-khian tinggal biasanya dililit kain satin berwarna, dan biksu melilitkan kain satin pada pohon tua untuk melindunginya dari penebangan; penebangan harus didahului upacara meminta izin.
statement.en: Trees housing Ta-khian are traditionally wrapped in coloured satin, and monks wrap old trees to protect them from logging; felling requires a ceremony to ask permission.

claims.quote: In some parts of Thailand, Nang Ta-khian has become a popular tree deity. Miracles are attributed to her power and not only living trees, but also logs, beams or keels of wooden boats where the spirit is deemed to reside are an object of pilgrimage

statement.id: Di sebagian Thailand, Nang Ta-khian menjadi dewi pohon populer; mukjizat dikaitkan dengannya, dan kayu, balok, atau lunas perahu yang diyakini dihuninya menjadi tempat ziarah; kini ia sering dipuja agar beruntung dalam lotre.
statement.en: In parts of Thailand, Nang Ta-khian has become a popular tree deity; miracles are credited to her, logs, beams or boat keels she is thought to inhabit are pilgrimage objects, and she is now often propitiated for lottery luck.

claims.quote: larger temples and shrines dedicated to Nang Ta-Khian are found in locations such as Sao Hai District, Saraburi Province and Amphawa District, Samut Songkhram Province

statement.id: Kuil besar untuk Nang Ta-khian ada antara lain di Distrik Sao Hai, Saraburi, dan Distrik Amphawa, Samut Songkhram.
statement.en: Larger shrines to Nang Ta-khian are in Sao Hai District, Saraburi, and Amphawa District, Samut Songkhram.

claims.quote: This folk spirit is featured in the 2003 Thai film Ta-khian ("The Haunted Tree"), with Sorapong Chatree

statement.id: Roh ini muncul dalam film Thai Ta-khian (The Haunted Tree, 2003) dengan Sorapong Chatree.
statement.en: This spirit features in the 2003 Thai film Ta-khian (The Haunted Tree) with Sorapong Chatree.

claims.quote: ต้นตะเคียนในวัฒนธรรมไทยก็ถูกอธิบายด้วยความเชื่อเรื่องสิ่ง ศักดิ์สิทธิ์และรุกขเทวดา โดยการปรับเปลี่ยนให้เป็นวิญญาณของผู้หญิงที่สิงในต้นตะเคียน
claims.locator: หัวข้อ ความเชื่อและการบูชาเจ้าแม่ตะเคียน

statement.id: Artikel jurnal ini menyatakan bahwa dalam budaya Thai pohon ta-khian dijelaskan lewat kepercayaan tentang hal-hal sakral dan dewa pohon (rukkhadeva), yang disesuaikan menjadi arwah perempuan yang bersemayam di pohon ta-khian.
statement.en: The journal article says that in Thai culture the ta-khian tree is explained through belief in sacred things and tree deities (rukkhadeva), adapted into the spirit of a woman dwelling in the ta-khian tree.

claims.quote: ในกรณีของนางตะเคียนหรือเจ้าแม่ตะเคียน เป็นความเชื่อท้องถิ่นที่ชาวบ้านเชื่อ ว่าต้นไม้ใหญ่จะมีรุกขเทวดาอาศัยอยู่

statement.id: Nang Ta-khian atau Chao Mae Ta-khian adalah kepercayaan setempat bahwa pohon besar dihuni dewa pohon (rukkhadeva).
statement.en: Nang Ta-khian, or Chao Mae Ta-khian, is a local belief that big trees are inhabited by tree deities (rukkhadeva).

claims.quote: ซึ่งกล่าวถึง “ผีนางตะเคียน” และการมีอยู่ของต้นตะเคียนในป่าช้า รวมทั้งคาบอกเล่าที่เชื่อกันว่าศพที่ ฝังใต้ร่มเงาต้นตะเคียนจะเป็นศพผีตายโหง และผีนางตะเคียนจะคอยควบคุมดูแล
claims.locator: หัวข้อ ความเชื่อและการบูชาเจ้าแม่ตะเคียน

statement.id: Menurut artikel ini, pohon ta-khian ada di pekuburan, dan dipercaya jenazah yang dikubur di bawah naungannya menjadi hantu yang mati tak wajar, yang diawasi oleh hantu Nang Ta-khian.
statement.en: According to the article, ta-khian trees stand in cemeteries, and bodies buried in their shade are believed to become ghosts of violent death, overseen by the ghost Nang Ta-khian.

claims.quote: มีเรื่องเล่าเกี่ยวกับเสาร้องไห้ ซึ่งต่อมาเป็นชื่ออาเภอเสาไห้ ในจังหวัดสระบุรี โดยเชื่อว่า เสาต้นตะเคียนที่มาจากแม่น้าป่าสักเป็นที่สิงสถิตของนางตะเคียน แต่เมื่อไม่ถูกเลือกให้เป็น เสาเอกสาหรับสร้างวังของกษัตริย์ในสมัยรัตนโกสินทร์ ก็เกิดความเสียใจจึงร้องไห้และลอย ทวนน้ากลับไปที่แม่น้าป่าสักตามเดิม
claims.locator: หัวข้อ ความเชื่อและการบูชาเจ้าแม่ตะเคียน

statement.id: Ada kisah "tiang yang menangis" yang kemudian menjadi nama distrik Sao Hai di Provinsi Saraburi: tiang kayu ta-khian dari Sungai Pa Sak dipercaya tempat bersemayam Nang Ta-khian; ketika tidak dipilih sebagai tiang utama istana raja pada masa Rattanakosin, ia bersedih, menangis, dan hanyut melawan arus kembali ke sungai tersebut.
statement.en: There is a tale of a "weeping pillar" that later gave its name to Sao Hai District in Saraburi Province: a ta-khian pillar from the Pa Sak River was believed to be Nang Ta-khian's dwelling; when it was not chosen as the main pillar of a king's palace in the Rattanakosin period, she grieved, wept and drifted upstream back to that river.

claims.quote: นอกจากนั้น การหลบลู่เจ้าแม่ตะเคียน เช่น การปัสสาวะรดตอต้นตะเคียนก็จะทาให้คน ๆ นั้นล้มป่วยโดยไม่ทราบสาเหตุ ถ้าจะให้หาย ป่วย จะต้องไปขอขมาด้วยเครื่องเซ่นเพื่อให้นางตะเคียนช่วยให้หายป่วย
claims.locator: หัวข้อ ความเชื่อและการบูชาเจ้าแม่ตะเคียน

statement.id: Orang yang tidak menghormati Chao Mae Ta-khian, misalnya mengencingi tunggul pohon ta-khian, dipercaya jatuh sakit tanpa sebab yang diketahui; untuk sembuh ia harus memohon maaf dengan sesajen agar Nang Ta-khian membantunya pulih.
statement.en: A person who shows disrespect to Chao Mae Ta-khian, for example by urinating on a ta-khian stump, is believed to fall ill for no known reason; to recover he must apologise with offerings so that Nang Ta-khian will help him get well.

claims.quote: ชี้ให้เห็นว่าในช่วงต้นรัตนโกสินทร์ การกราบ ไหว้บูชาเจ้าแม่ตะเคียนในฐานะเป็นรุกขเทวดาและนางไม้ที่ศักดิ์สิทธิ์และมีความน่ากลัว เป็น เรื่องที่พบเห็นได้ทั่วไปในท้องถิ่น ซึ่งซากต้นตะเคียนที่จมอยู่ในแม่น้าจะถูกนามาบูชาด้วย เครื่องเซ่นสังเวยพร้อมสร้างศาลเพียงตาเพื่อให้นางตะเคียนช่วยคุ้มครองป้องกันและดล บันดาลให้ประสบความสาเร็จในสิ่งที่ต้องการ
claims.locator: หัวข้อ ความเชื่อและการบูชาเจ้าแม่ตะเคียน

statement.id: Menurut artikel ini, pada awal periode Rattanakosin pemujaan Chao Mae Ta-khian sebagai dewa pohon dan peri pohon yang sakral dan menakutkan lazim ditemui di daerah; sisa pohon ta-khian yang tenggelam di sungai dipuja dengan sesajen dan altar kecil agar Nang Ta-khian melindungi dan memberi keberhasilan.
statement.en: According to the article, in the early Rattanakosin period worship of Chao Mae Ta-khian as a sacred and fearsome tree deity and tree nymph was commonly seen locally; remains of ta-khian trees sunk in rivers were worshipped with offerings and a small shrine so that Nang Ta-khian would protect people and grant success.

claims.quote: ไม้ตะเคียนที่นาไปทาเป็นเสาเรือนและมีน้ามันไหลซึมออกมา ชาวบ้านเรียกว่า “เสาตกน้ามัน” ซึ่งเชื่อว่าเป็นที่สิงสถิตของวิญญาณของผีนางตะเคียน มีความเฮี้ยน เจ้าของบ้านจะนาเครื่องเซ่นไหว้มาบูชาเสาตกน้ามัน เพื่อให้ผีนางตะเคียนคุ้มครองและดูแล บ้าน
claims.locator: หัวข้อ ความเชื่อและการบูชาเจ้าแม่ตะเคียน

statement.id: Kayu ta-khian yang dijadikan tiang rumah dan mengeluarkan getah minyak disebut "tiang yang menetes minyak"; dipercaya menjadi tempat bersemayam Nang Ta-khian, dan pemilik rumah menyajikan sesajen agar ia melindungi dan menjaga rumah.
statement.en: Ta-khian wood made into a house post that oozes oil is called an "oil-dripping post"; it is believed to house Nang Ta-khian, and the owner presents offerings so that she will protect and look after the house.

claims.quote: หากพิจารณาการเปลี่ยนฐานะของนางตะเคียนที่เป็นนางไม้ไปสู่การเป็นเจ้าแม่ อาจดูได้จากเหตุการณ์ที่นางตะเคียนมาเข้าฝันมนุษย์ และบอกให้นาต้นตะเคียนที่จมอยู่ใน น้าหรือในบ่อขึ้นมา เพื่อที่จะทาให้นางตะเคียนมีที่อยู่ที่สบายกว่าเดิม
claims.locator: หัวข้อ ความเชื่อและการบูชาเจ้าแม่ตะเคียน

statement.id: Artikel ini membahas peralihan status Nang Ta-khian dari peri pohon menjadi dewi (chao mae), yang terlihat dari kisah ia muncul dalam mimpi dan meminta batang ta-khian yang terendam diangkat agar ia mendapat tempat tinggal yang lebih nyaman.
statement.en: The article discusses Nang Ta-khian's change of status from tree nymph to a goddess (chao mae), seen in accounts of her appearing in dreams and asking for the submerged ta-khian log to be raised so she has a more comfortable dwelling.

claims.quote: It is found that Ta-Khian Goddess is culturally embodied as “beautiful woman” under the implicit power/knowledge structure of nationalism, rationalism and capitalism stabilized Thai society since 1960s.

statement.id: Abstrak artikel menyatakan bahwa Dewi Ta-khian secara budaya diwujudkan sebagai "perempuan cantik" di bawah struktur kuasa/pengetahuan nasionalisme, rasionalisme, dan kapitalisme yang mapan dalam masyarakat Thai sejak 1960-an.
statement.en: The article's abstract states that the Ta-Khian Goddess is culturally embodied as a "beautiful woman" under the power/knowledge structure of nationalism, rationalism and capitalism that has been stable in Thai society since the 1960s.

claims.quote: Moreover, the ritual worship of sacred Ta-Khian Goddess found in local communities indicates the adaptive consolidation in which modernity and superstition are merged.

statement.id: Abstrak yang sama menyatakan bahwa ritual pemujaan Dewi Ta-khian di komunitas lokal menunjukkan perpaduan modernitas dan kepercayaan takhayul.
statement.en: The same abstract states that the ritual worship of the Ta-Khian Goddess in local communities shows a merging of modernity and superstition.

claims.quote: We collected data 10 provinces along the Chaophraya riparian area. ... As the result, the big Hopea odorata was 164 trees and 81 trees were the spiritual trees.

statement.id: Abstrak penelitian ini menyebut pengumpulan data di 10 provinsi sepanjang tepi Sungai Chao Phraya, dengan hasil 164 pohon Hopea odorata besar, 81 di antaranya pohon keramat (spiritual trees).
statement.en: The abstract reports data collected in 10 provinces along the Chaophraya riparian area, finding 164 big Hopea odorata trees, 81 of which were spiritual trees.

claims.quote: The spiritual culture combines the pray with Takhian Goddess for successful of things. As they got the successful things and then they had stuffs for Ta-khian Goddess. The stuff values of spiritual culture were 257,030 THB that most from traditional Thai dress.

statement.id: Abstrak yang sama menyatakan bahwa orang berdoa kepada Dewi Ta-khian dan, bila berhasil, memberikan persembahan, yang bernilai 257.030 baht dan sebagian besar berupa pakaian tradisional Thai.
statement.en: The same abstract states that people pray to the Ta-khian Goddess and, once successful, give offerings worth 257,030 THB, mostly traditional Thai dress.

claims.quote: ประเภทนางไม้ พบใน นิราศเมืองแกลง โคลงนิราศฉะเชิงเทรา และ นิราศปราจีนบุรี ได้แก่ นางตะเคียนและนางไม้ในป่า โดยที่กวีไม่ได้ระบุชื่อ

statement.id: Abstrak artikel tentang kepercayaan dewa pohon dan peri pohon dalam puisi perjalanan (nirat) menyebut peri pohon, yaitu Nang Ta-khian dan peri hutan yang tak dinamai penyairnya, dalam Nirat Mueang Klaeng, Khlong Nirat Chachoengsao, dan Nirat Prachinburi.
statement.en: The abstract of an article on tree-deity and tree-nymph beliefs in travel poems (nirat) reports tree nymphs, namely Nang Ta-khian and forest tree nymphs whom the poet did not name, in Nirat Mueang Klaeng, Khlong Nirat Chachoengsao and Nirat Prachinburi.

claims.quote: However, in present times some of these very ancient trees are felled anyway for their wood, even though it is said to be dangerous for a person to cut such a tree without the previous consent of the spirit inhabiting it.

statement.id: Pada masa kini sebagian pohon sangat tua itu tetap ditebang untuk diambil kayunya, meskipun konon berbahaya menebang pohon tersebut tanpa persetujuan roh penghuninya.
statement.en: In present times some of these very ancient trees are felled anyway for their wood, even though it is said to be dangerous to cut such a tree without the consent of the spirit inhabiting it.

claims.quote: Nang Ta-khian is generally a sylvan spirit, for the Ta-khian is a tall, massive tree that can live for centuries, naturally found in the forest and not near inhabited areas.

statement.id: Nang Ta-khian umumnya roh hutan, karena ta-khian adalah pohon tinggi dan besar yang bisa hidup berabad-abad dan tumbuh alami di hutan, bukan di dekat permukiman.
statement.en: Nang Ta-khian is generally a sylvan spirit, because the ta-khian is a tall, massive tree that can live for centuries and grows naturally in forests, not near inhabited areas.

claims.quote: 2010 movie Nang Ta-khian ("Takien: The Haunted Tree") and 2025 Channel 8 lakhon "Love Across Lifetimes" (พิศวาสข้ามภพ). Nang Ta-khian has a role as well in the Nak animated movie.

statement.id: Selain film 2003, Nang Ta-khian muncul dalam film 2010 Nang Ta-khian ("Takien: The Haunted Tree") dan lakhon Channel 8 2025 "Love Across Lifetimes", serta berperan dalam film animasi Nak.
statement.en: Besides the 2003 film, Nang Ta-khian appears in the 2010 movie Nang Ta-khian ("Takien: The Haunted Tree") and the 2025 Channel 8 lakhon "Love Across Lifetimes", and has a role in the Nak animated movie.

text.id: Tokoh novel abad ke-16; sudah muncul dalam drama zaju dinasti Yuan sebelumnya
text.en: Character of a 16th-century novel; she already appears in an earlier Yuan dynasty zaju play

short_description.id: Princess Iron Fan (Tieshan Gongzhu) adalah iblis perempuan atau raksasi (Rākṣasī) dalam novel Journey to the West. Ia istri Bull Demon King, ibu Red Boy, dan pemilik kipas pisang yang bisa memadamkan api dan mengibaskan orang jauh-jauh.
short_description.en: Princess Iron Fan (Tieshan Gongzhu) is a demoness, or female rakshasa (Rākṣasī), in the novel Journey to the West. She is the wife of Bull Demon King, the mother of Red Boy, and the owner of a banana-leaf fan that puts out fire and blows people far away.

long_description.id: Princess Iron Fan adalah tokoh sastra dari novel Tiongkok abad ke-16 Journey to the West (Perjalanan ke Barat). Wikipedia menyebutnya iblis perempuan yang cantik, istri Bull Demon King, dan ibu Red Boy. Dalam novel ia juga disebut Luocha Nü (羅剎女), yaitu Rākṣasī, sehingga wujudnya adalah raksasi, bukan manusia biasa.
long_description.en: Princess Iron Fan is a literary character from the 16th-century Chinese novel Journey to the West. Wikipedia calls her a beautiful demoness, the wife of Bull Demon King, and the mother of Red Boy. In the novel she is also called Luocha Nü (羅剎女), that is Rākṣasī, so she is a female rakshasa rather than an ordinary human.

long_description.id: Ia memiliki kipas pisang (芭蕉扇). Menurut novel, kipas itu bila dimohon memadamkan api dengan satu kibasan, membangkitkan angin dengan dua, dan menurunkan hujan dengan tiga. Orang yang terkena kibasannya terbawa delapan puluh empat ribu li. Ketika Sun Wukong datang untuk meminjamnya, ia bertarung dengannya dan menyapu Sun Wukong dengan kibasan itu. Dalam bab yang sama Sun Wukong juga berkata bahwa ia sudah berada di dalam perutnya.
long_description.en: She owns a banana-leaf fan (芭蕉扇). According to the novel, the fan, if obtained, puts out fire with one fanning, raises wind with two, and brings rain with three. A person fanned by it is carried eighty-four thousand li. When Sun Wukong comes to borrow it, she fights him and sweeps him away with the fan. In the same chapter Sun Wukong also says he is already inside her belly.

long_description.id: Menurut dewa bumi dalam novel, suaminya telah meninggalkannya dan tinggal di Gua Moyun di Gunung Jilei, tempat Yumian Gongzhu berada. Dalam bab berikutnya, setelah para dewa menaklukkan suaminya, ia keluar membawa kipas dan menyerahkannya kepada Sun Wukong; ia juga memberi tahu bahwa kipas itu harus dikibaskan 49 kali untuk memutus akar api.
long_description.en: According to the earth deity in the novel, her husband has abandoned her and lives at Moyun Cave on Jilei Mountain, where Yumian Gongzhu lives. In the following chapter, after the gods subdue her husband, she comes out with the fan and hands it to Sun Wukong; she also tells him the fan must be waved 49 times to cut the root of the fire.

cultural_context.id: Di luar novel Journey to the West, Wikipedia mencatat bahwa dalam Journey to the South ia digambarkan sebagai dewi, dan ia dipuja bersama Huaguang Dadi di Kuil Huaguang Great Emperor.
cultural_context.en: Beyond the novel Journey to the West, Wikipedia records that in Journey to the South she is depicted as a goddess, and that she is worshipped alongside Huaguang Dadi in the Huaguang Great Emperor Temple.

who.id: Iblis perempuan atau raksasi dalam novel Journey to the West.
who.en: A demoness, or female rakshasa, in the novel Journey to the West.

origin.id: Novel Tiongkok abad ke-16 Journey to the West.

role.id: Pemilik kipas pisang yang dicari Sun Wukong untuk memadamkan api Flaming Mountains.
role.en: The owner of the banana-leaf fan that Sun Wukong seeks in order to put out the fire of the Flaming Mountains.

famous_for.id: Kipas pisang yang bisa memadamkan api dan mengibaskan orang sejauh delapan puluh empat ribu li.
famous_for.en: The banana-leaf fan that can put out fire and blow a person eighty-four thousand li.

did_you_know.id: Menurut Wikipedia, film animasi panjang Tiongkok pertama, Princess Iron Fan (1941), mengadaptasi pertemuan Sun Wukong dengannya.
did_you_know.en: According to Wikipedia, the first Chinese animated feature film, Princess Iron Fan (1941), adapts Sun Wukong's encounter with her.

description.id: Satu kibasan memadamkan api, dua membangkitkan angin, tiga menurunkan hujan; kibasan angin dinginnya juga menyapu Sun Wukong hingga tak terlihat, dan orang yang terkena terbawa delapan puluh empat ribu li.
description.en: One fanning puts out fire, two raise wind, three bring rain; its cold wind also sweeps Sun Wukong out of sight, and a person fanned is carried eighty-four thousand li.

description.en: In that play she identifies herself as an immortal who had been an ancestor of the Wind Department; the play predates her appearance as the wife of Bull Demon King in the novel.

title.id: Meminjam kipas pisang dari Princess Iron Fan
title.en: Borrowing the banana-leaf fan from Princess Iron Fan

role.id: Pemilik kipas yang menolak meminjamkannya kepada Sun Wukong, sampai akhirnya menyerahkannya.
role.en: The owner of the fan who refuses to lend it to Sun Wukong until she finally hands it over.

summary.id: Sun Wukong mendatangi Gua Pisang di Gunung Cuiyun untuk meminjam kipas. Luocha Nü bertarung dengannya dan menyapunya dengan kipas, dan Sun Wukong berkata bahwa ia sudah berada di dalam perutnya. Pada akhirnya, setelah para dewa menaklukkan suaminya, ia menyerahkan kipas itu dan menjelaskan cara memutus akar api.
summary.en: Sun Wukong goes to the Banana Cave on Cuiyun Mountain to borrow the fan. Luocha Nü fights him and sweeps him away with the fan, and Sun Wukong says he is already inside her belly. In the end, after the gods subdue her husband, she hands over the fan and explains how to cut the root of the fire.

description.en: The dwelling of Tieshan Xian in the novel, sought out by Sun Wukong to borrow the fan.

statement.id: Dalam novel, seorang penebang kayu menyebut bahwa yang ada adalah Tieshan Gongzhu (鐵扇公主), juga bernama Luocha Nü (羅剎女), pemilik kipas pisang (芭蕉扇) yang bisa memadamkan Flaming Mountains (火焰山) dan istri Bull Demon King (大力牛魔王).
statement.en: In the novel, a woodcutter says that the one who lives there is Tieshan Gongzhu (鐵扇公主), also called Luocha Nü (羅剎女), owner of a banana-leaf fan (芭蕉扇) able to extinguish the Flaming Mountains (火焰山) and wife of the mighty Bull Demon King (大力牛魔王).

statement.en: In the novel, a man explains that the banana-leaf fan (芭蕉扇) of Tieshan Xian (鐵扇仙), if obtained, puts out fire with one fanning, raises wind with two, and brings rain with three.

statement.en: In the novel, after fighting Sun Wukong (行者) until evening, Luocha Nü (羅剎女) takes out the banana-leaf fan (芭蕉扇) and one fanning of its cold wind sweeps Sun Wukong out of sight.

statement.en: In the novel, Luocha Nü (羅剎) comes out carrying the banana-leaf fan (芭蕉扇), twelve chi long; seeing the gods, she kneels and begs for the couple's lives, offering the fan to Sun Wukong (孫叔叔).

statement.id: Dalam novel, Nezha (哪吒) menggantungkan roda api di tanduk Bull Demon King (牛王), dan Heavenly King Li (托塔天王) menahan wujud aslinya dengan cermin 照妖鏡 hingga ia tak bisa lari dan menyatakan bersedia tunduk pada ajaran Buddha.

short_description.id: Abura-akago adalah yōkai yang digambar sebagai bayi peminum minyak lampu; sosoknya dikaitkan dengan cerita lama tentang api dari roh pencuri minyak.
short_description.en: Abura-akago is a yōkai depicted as a baby drinking lamp oil, linked to an older tale of a fire arising from the spirit of an oil thief.

long_description.id: Abura-akago, secara harfiah “bayi minyak”, tampak dalam ilustrasi Toriyama Sekien sebagai bayi yang menjilat minyak lampu andon. Catatan yang menyertainya menyebut bola api yang terbang di Ōtsu. Dalam cerita lebih lama tentang api pencuri minyak, seorang penjual minyak di Shiga dikisahkan mengambil minyak dari arca Jizō dan setelah wafat rohnya menjadi api yang berkeliaran. Basis data penelitian cerita rakyat juga mencatat cerita tentang pencuri minyak dan api itu, terpisah dari wujud bayi dalam ilustrasi Sekien.
long_description.en: Abura-akago, literally “oil baby,” appears in Toriyama Sekien’s illustration as a baby licking oil from an andon lamp. Its accompanying text mentions a flying ball of fire in Ōtsu. An older account of the oil-stealing fire tells of a merchant in Shiga who stole oil from a Jizō image and whose spirit became a wandering flame after death. A folklore research database also records that oil-thief story separately from the baby form in Sekien’s picture.

long_description.id: Catatan Sekien menanyakan apakah bayi penjilat minyak itu mungkin kelahiran kembali si pencuri. Literatur yōkai yang lebih baru menggambarkannya berubah dari bola api menjadi bayi peminum minyak lampu lalu kembali menjadi api. Gambaran tersebut berasal dari tafsir yang lebih baru atas cerita api yang lebih tua.
long_description.en: Sekien’s note asks whether the oil-licking baby might be the thief reborn. Later yōkai literature depicts it changing from a fireball into a baby that drinks lamp oil and back into fire. That portrayal is a later interpretation of the older fire tale.

claims.quote: Abura-akago (油赤子; "oil baby") is a type of Japanese infant spirit or ghost. It is a yōkai that appeared illustrated in Toriyama Sekien's mid-Edo period Konjaku Gazu Zoku Hyakki, as an infant spirit lapping oil out of an andon lamp.

statement.id: Abura-akago berarti bayi minyak dan digambar Sekien sebagai bayi yōkai yang menjilat minyak lampu.
statement.en: Abura-akago means oil baby and was drawn by Sekien as a baby yōkai licking lamp oil.

statement.en: Sekien’s text mentions a flying ball of fire in Ōtsu.

claims.quote: The natives say that long ago in the village of Shiga there was an oil merchant, and every night he stole the oil from the Jizō of the Ōtsu crossroads, but when this person died his soul became a flame

statement.en: An older tale tells of an oil thief whose spirit became a flame after death.

claims.quote: Sekien's accompanying notes describe it: ... If it is so, then the baby who licks the oil is this person's rebirth.

short_description.id: Akabeko adalah sapi merah misterius dalam legenda Aizu yang membantu pembangunan Kuil Enzoji. Kisahnya mengilhami mainan rakyat setempat.
short_description.en: Akabeko is a mysterious red cow in an Aizu legend that helped build Enzoji Temple. Its story inspired a local folk toy.

long_description.id: Salah satu cerita asal-usul Akabeko berpusat pada pembangunan Kuil Enzoji di Aizu. Menurut cerita itu, seekor sapi merah yang tidak dikenal muncul, memimpin ternak lain, dan terus bekerja sampai pengangkutan bahan bangunan selesai. Penduduk yang berterima kasih kemudian mendirikan arca sapi tersebut di lingkungan kuil.
long_description.en: One origin story places Akabeko at the building of Enzoji Temple in Aizu. In this account, an unknown red cow appeared, led the other cattle, and worked until the transport of building materials was finished. Grateful residents then erected statues of the cow in the temple grounds.

long_description.id: Cerita sapi itu kemudian menjadi dasar pembuatan mainan kecil Akabeko di Aizu. Mainan dari bubur kertas tersebut memiliki kepala yang dapat bergoyang. Dalam tradisi setempat, mainan ini juga dipandang sebagai pembawa keberuntungan dan pelindung dari penyakit.
long_description.en: The cow story later inspired small Akabeko toys in Aizu. These papier-mâché toys have bobbing heads. In local tradition, the toys have also been regarded as good-luck charms and protection from illness.

cultural_context.id: Arca sapi dalam kisah Akabeko dikaitkan dengan kesehatan dan keberuntungan; mainannya dipakai sebagai jimat saat wabah cacar.
cultural_context.en: The cow statues in the Akabeko story came to be associated with health and fortune; its toys served as charms during a smallpox outbreak.

short_description.id: Apsonsi adalah makhluk mitologi Thai berwujud setengah perempuan setengah singa, yang diyakini sebagai pelindung dan patungnya menjaga Wat Phra Kaew di Bangkok.
short_description.en: The apsonsi is a half-woman, half-lion creature of Thai mythology, believed to protect from harm, whose statues guard Wat Phra Kaew in Bangkok.

long_description.id: Apsonsi adalah makhluk mitologi Thai berwujud setengah perempuan dan setengah singa, salah satu dari banyak makhluk campuran dalam cerita rakyat kuno Asia Selatan dan Tenggara. Namanya, yang juga dieja Apsonsingh atau Apsarasingha, adalah gabungan apsara (bidadari) dan singha (singa); dalam bahasa Thai apsara dikenal sebagai apson. Gabungan malaikat laki-laki dan singa disebut Thepnorasi, dan apsonsi dapat dibandingkan dengan Manussiha, makhluk setengah singa setengah manusia dari Myanmar.
long_description.en: The apsonsi is a half-woman, half-lion creature of Thai mythology, one of many hybrid beings in ancient South and Southeast Asian folklore. Its name, also spelled Apsonsingh or Apsarasingha, combines apsara (a female nymph) and singha (a lion); in Thai, apsara is known as apson. The male angel-and-lion combination is called Thepnorasi, and the apsonsi is comparable to the Manussiha, a half-lion, half-man creature of Myanmar.

long_description.id: Menurut legenda, apsonsi tinggal di Himavanta, hutan mitos tak kasatmata yang terletak jauh di pegunungan Himalaya. Himavanta digambarkan sebagai hutan suci di puncak Gunung Himmapan, tempat tinggal para dewa dan makhluk mitos. Apsonsi diyakini sebagai pelindung dari marabahaya, dan patung-patungnya berjaga di Wat Phra Kaew, Kuil Buddha Zamrud, di Bangkok.
long_description.en: According to legend, the apsonsi lived in Himavanta, an invisible mythical forest deep in the Himalaya mountains. Himavanta is described as a sacred forest atop Himmapan Mountain, home to gods and mythical creatures. The apsonsi is believed to protect from harm, and its statues stand guard at Wat Phra Kaew, the Temple of the Emerald Buddha, in Bangkok.

long_description.id: Sebuah plakat di Los Angeles menyebut apsonsi, atau "malaikat Thai", sebagai pelindung dari marabahaya dalam sastra Thai kuno, dan sumber lain tentang Thai Town mencatat bahwa makhluk ini dikatakan melindungi dan membawa keberuntungan. Dua patung dipasang di perempatan Hollywood Boulevard dan Western Avenue sebagai gerbang Thai Town, dan dua lagi di ujung timurnya; plakat menyebut patung-patung itu berdiri di empat sudut Thai Town sebagai penjaga simbolis dan merupakan hadiah dari Pemerintah Kerajaan Thailand.
long_description.en: A plaque in Los Angeles describes the apsonsi, or "Thai angels", as protectors against harm in ancient Thai literature, and another source on Thai Town notes that the creature is said to protect and bring good luck. Two statues were installed at the intersection of Hollywood Boulevard and Western Avenue as a gateway to Thai Town, and another two at its eastern end; the plaque says the statues stand at the four corners of Thai Town as symbolic guardians and were a gift from the Royal Thai Government.

statement.id: Dalam kepercayaan Buddha, keberadaan Himavanta dan makhluk mitosnya bukan ancaman bagi manusia, karena hanya orang yang berbudi dan rohani yang dapat memasukinya.
statement.en: In Buddhist belief, the existence of Himavanta and its mythical creatures is no threat to humans, since only virtuous and spiritual people can enter it.

claims.quote: Apsaras ... are a class of celestial beings in Hindu and Buddhist culture. They were originally a type of female spirit associated with clouds and water, but, later came to play the role of a "nymph" or "fairy".

statement.id: Apsara adalah golongan makhluk langit dalam budaya Hindu dan Buddha; awalnya semacam roh perempuan yang berkaitan dengan awan dan air, lalu berperan sebagai "nimfa" atau "peri".
statement.en: Apsaras are a class of celestial beings in Hindu and Buddhist culture, originally a type of female spirit associated with clouds and water, later playing the role of a "nymph" or "fairy".

claims.quote: and In Thai: อัปสร (RTGS: Apson).

statement.id: Dalam bahasa Thai, apsara dikenal sebagai อัปสร (RTGS: Apson).
statement.en: In Thai, apsara is known as อัปสร (RTGS: Apson).

claims.quote: Manussiha ... is a Burmese half-man half-lion mythical creature believed to be created by Buddhist missionary monks to protect a new-born royal baby from being devoured by rakshasis (ogresses) from the sea. Its statues are usually found guarding the four corners of a pagoda.

statement.id: Manussiha adalah makhluk mitos Burma setengah manusia setengah singa yang diyakini diciptakan para biksu misionaris Buddha untuk melindungi bayi kerajaan yang baru lahir dari rakshasi (raksasi) dari laut; patungnya biasanya menjaga empat sudut pagoda.
statement.en: Manussiha is a Burmese half-man half-lion mythical creature believed to have been created by Buddhist missionary monks to protect a newborn royal baby from rakshasis (ogresses) from the sea; its statues usually guard the four corners of a pagoda.

claims.quote: kinnaris, the female counterpart of kinnaras, are depicted as half-bird, half-woman creatures. One of the many creatures that inhabit the mythical Himavanta, kinnaris have the head, torso, and arms of a woman and the wings, tail and feet of a swan.

statement.id: Dalam mitologi Buddha Asia Tenggara, kinnari digambarkan sebagai makhluk setengah burung setengah perempuan, salah satu penghuni Himavanta yang mitos, berkepala, berbadan, dan berlengan perempuan dengan sayap, ekor, dan kaki angsa.
statement.en: In Southeast Asian Buddhist mythology, kinnaris are depicted as half-bird, half-woman creatures, one of the many inhabitants of the mythical Himavanta, with the head, torso and arms of a woman and the wings, tail and feet of a swan.

text.id: Kisahnya dipercaya berlatar masa Raja Rama IV, atau awal periode Rattanakosin.
text.en: The story is believed to be set in the reign of King Rama IV, or the early Rattanakosin period.

short_description.id: Mae Nak Phra Khanong adalah hantu paling terkenal di Thailand: seorang istri yang meninggal saat melahirkan tetapi tetap menunggu suaminya pulang dari perang dan menyamar sebagai istri yang masih hidup.
short_description.en: Mae Nak Phra Khanong is Thailand's best-known ghost: a wife who died in childbirth yet kept waiting for her husband to return from war, living on as if she were still alive.

long_description.id: Mae Nak Phra Khanong, atau Mae Nak dan Nang Nak, adalah hantu Thailand yang sangat terkenal. Menurut cerita rakyat setempat, kisahnya berdasarkan peristiwa pada masa pemerintahan Raja Rama IV. Mae Nak tinggal di tepi Kanal Phra Khanong dan sangat mencintai suaminya, Mak.
long_description.en: Mae Nak Phra Khanong, also Mae Nak or Nang Nak, is a famous Thai ghost. According to local folklore, her story is based on events in the reign of King Rama IV. Mae Nak lived on the Phra Khanong Canal and deeply loved her husband, Mak.

long_description.id: Ketika Nak hamil, Mak dikirim berperang dan terluka parah. Selama Mak dirawat, Nak dan bayinya meninggal saat persalinan, tetapi ketika Mak pulang, istri dan anaknya menyambutnya. Suatu hari Nak menjatuhkan jeruk nipis dari beranda dan menjulurkan lengannya sangat panjang untuk memungutnya; Mak pun sadar istrinya hantu dan melarikan diri ke Wat Mahabut, tanah suci yang tak bisa dimasuki hantu.
long_description.en: While Nak was pregnant, Mak was sent to war and badly wounded. While he recovered, Nak and their child died in childbirth, yet when Mak came home his wife and child greeted him. One day Nak dropped a lime from the porch and stretched her arm to an impossible length to pick it up; Mak realized she was a ghost and fled to Wat Mahabut, holy ground a ghost cannot enter.

long_description.id: Dalam kesedihannya, Nak meneror warga Phra Khanong. Menurut satu versi, seorang biksu sakti menangkap arwahnya dalam guci tanah liat dan membuangnya ke kanal. Dalam versi lain, biksu Somdet Phra Phutthachan (Somdej Toh) membimbing Nak dengan welas asih hingga ia rela melepaskan kehidupan lamanya, lalu menyimpan sepotong tulang dahinya sebagai jimat.
long_description.en: In her grief, Nak terrorized the people of Phra Khanong. In one version, a powerful monk captured her spirit in an earthen jar and threw it into the canal. In another, the monk Somdet Phra Phutthachan (Somdej Toh) guided Nak with compassion until she let go of her past life, and kept a piece of her forehead bone as an amulet.

long_description.id: Sejarawan Anek Nawikamul menemukan artikel surat kabar tahun 1899 yang menyebut kisah ini berdasarkan kehidupan Amdaeng Nak, yang meninggal saat hamil; putranya konon mengarang cerita hantu itu agar ayahnya tidak menikah lagi. Kini kuil Mae Nak di Wat Mahabut ramai dikunjungi, terutama oleh perempuan yang memohon persalinan lancar dan orang yang berharap suaminya lolos wajib militer.
long_description.en: Historian Anek Nawikamul found an 1899 newspaper article claiming the story was based on the life of Amdaeng Nak, who died while pregnant; her son supposedly invented the ghost tale so his father would not remarry. Today Mae Nak's shrine at Wat Mahabut draws many visitors, especially women seeking an easy childbirth and people hoping their husbands avoid conscription.

long_description.id: Dalam budaya populer, The Nation menyebut Mae Nak sebagai hantu perempuan Thai yang terkenal dan dipopulerkan dalam banyak serial TV, sandiwara, dan film, terutama film horor supranatural Nang Nak tahun 1999 yang dibintangi aktris Intira "Sai" Jaroenpura. Thai PBS NOW juga menyebut kisah แม่นากพระโขนง secara khusus di antara karya film dan drama. Sebuah ulasan buku di jurnal Thai mencantumkan ผีนางนาคพระโขนง di antara hantu-hantu Thai yang dibahas.
long_description.en: In popular culture, The Nation describes Mae Nak as a famous Thai female ghost who became widely known through many TV series, plays and films, above all the 1999 supernatural horror film Nang Nak, in which the actress Intira "Sai" Jaroenpura plays Nak. Thai PBS NOW also names the tale of แม่นากพระโขนง in particular among films and dramas. A book review in a Thai journal lists ผีนางนาคพระโขนง among the Thai ghosts covered.

cultural_context.id: Kisah Mae Nak juga dipandang sebagai gambaran ajaran Buddha tentang samsara dan tiga corak keberadaan: ketidakkekalan, penderitaan, dan tanpa-diri.
cultural_context.en: The Mae Nak story is also seen as illustrating Buddhist teachings on samsara and the three marks of existence: impermanence, suffering and non-self.

claims.quote: lit. 'Lady Nak of Phra Khanong'), or simply Mae Nak (แม่นาก, 'Lady Nak') or Nang Nak (นางนาก, 'Miss Nak'), is a well-known Thai ghost. According to local folklore the story is based on events that took place during the reign of King Rama IV.

statement.id: Mae Nak Phra Khanong (แม่นากพระโขนง, 'Nyonya Nak dari Phra Khanong'), atau Mae Nak dan Nang Nak, adalah hantu Thailand yang terkenal; menurut cerita rakyat, kisahnya berdasarkan peristiwa pada masa Raja Rama IV.
statement.en: Mae Nak Phra Khanong (แม่นากพระโขนง, 'Lady Nak of Phra Khanong'), or Mae Nak and Nang Nak, is a well-known Thai ghost; folklore says her story is based on events in King Rama IV's reign.

claims.quote: A shrine dedicated to Nak was constructed at Wat Mahabut. In 1997, the shrine was relocated to the nearby Suan Luang district of modern Bangkok.

statement.id: Kuil untuk Nak dibangun di Wat Mahabut dan pada 1997 dipindahkan ke distrik Suan Luang, Bangkok.
statement.en: A shrine to Nak was built at Wat Mahabut and in 1997 relocated to Suan Luang district, Bangkok.

claims.quote: While Nak was pregnant, Mak was conscripted into the Thai Army and sent to war where he was seriously wounded

statement.id: Ketika Nak hamil, Mak dikirim berperang dan terluka parah.

claims.quote: In her haste to retrieve it, she stretched her arm to an impossible length to pick it up from the ground below. Upon seeing this, Mak realised his wife was a ghost.

statement.id: Nak menjulurkan lengannya sangat panjang untuk memungut jeruk nipis dari tanah, dan Mak pun sadar istrinya hantu; ia lalu melarikan diri ke Wat Mahabut yang tak bisa dimasuki hantu.
statement.en: Nak stretched her arm to an impossible length to pick up a lime, and Mak realized she was a ghost; he then fled to Wat Mahabut, which ghosts cannot enter.

claims.quote: In her grief, Nak terrorised the people of Phra Khanong, furious at them for causing Mak to leave her. However, a powerful monk captured Nak's ghost; and after confining her in an earthen jar, threw it into the Phra Khanong canal.

statement.id: Nak yang berduka meneror warga Phra Khanong; seorang biksu sakti menangkap arwahnya, mengurungnya dalam guci tanah liat, dan membuangnya ke kanal.

claims.quote: In another, the monk assured Nak that in a future life she would be reunited with her beloved husband, so she voluntarily departed for the afterlife.

statement.id: Dalam versi lain, biksu meyakinkan Nak bahwa ia akan bersatu kembali dengan suaminya di kehidupan mendatang, sehingga ia rela pergi ke alam baka.
statement.en: In another version, the monk assured Nak she would be reunited with her husband in a future life, so she willingly departed.

claims.quote: Kulap claimed the story of Mae Nak was based on the life of Amdaeng Nak (Thai: อำแดงนาก, lit. 'Mrs Nak'), daughter of a Tambon Phra Khanong leader named Khun Si. Amdaeng Nak died while she was pregnant.

statement.id: Dalam artikel Siam Prabheth tahun 1899 yang ditemukan sejarawan Anek Nawikamul, K.S.R. Kulap menyebut kisah Mae Nak berdasarkan kehidupan Amdaeng Nak, putri pemimpin Phra Khanong bernama Khun Si, yang meninggal saat hamil.

claims.quote: Believed to date back to the early Rattanakosin period (around the 18th century), the legend has it that Mae Nak (“Mae” was used for “Miss” in those days) lived in the area near Wat Mahabut along a canal.

statement.id: Legenda yang diyakini berasal dari awal periode Rattanakosin ini menyebut Mae Nak tinggal di dekat Wat Mahabut di tepi kanal.
statement.en: The legend, believed to date to the early Rattanakosin period, says Mae Nak lived near Wat Mahabut beside a canal.

claims.quote: making her a “Pee tai tang klom” (ghost of a woman who died during childbirth with the baby still inside her). Her body was buried in the cemetery at Wat Mahabut. statement.en: Nak became a pee tai tang klom (ghost of a woman who died in childbirth with the baby inside); out of love her spirit stayed bound to her old life, appearing in human form to do the housework.

claims.quote: The venerable father then cremated Nak’s body and carved out a piece of her forehead bone to keep as an amulet.

statement.en: Prince Damrong recalled asking Wat Phra Kaeo visitors as a child who was most popular, and most answered Mae Nak.

On the raised wooden veranda of her old canal-side home (c09), one normal hand supports her while her OTHER ARM stretches to an IMPOSSIBLE several-metre LENGTH as a single anatomically continuous arm down from veranda to a small GREEN LIME on the ground (c04). Only one elbow and one hand on stretched arm, no branching limbs or giant finger tendrils. Show entire long curving arm from shoulder to hand and lime so uncanny tale reads immediately. Grieving watchful face turns towards viewer, body proportion normal but impossible arm unmistakably ghostly. Natural night side-light, dark canal below, sorrowful eerie horror without monstrous added teeth or skin, blood or extra babies. No aura or energy effects.

short_description.id: Rangda adalah ratu para leak dalam mitologi Bali, sosok janda menyeramkan yang dalam tari Barong melambangkan kekuatan jahat yang selalu bertarung dengan Barong.
short_description.en: Rangda is the queen of the leyaks in Balinese mythology, a terrifying widow figure who in the Barong dance embodies the evil forces forever battling the Barong.

long_description.id: Menurut mitologi tradisional Bali, Rangda adalah ratu iblis para leak. Ia memimpin pasukan penyihir jahat melawan Barong, pemimpin kekuatan baik, dan pertarungan keduanya ditampilkan dalam tari Barong sebagai lambang pertempuran abadi antara baik dan jahat. Namanya berasal dari bahasa Jawa Kuno yang berarti janda.
long_description.en: According to traditional Balinese mythology, Rangda is the demon queen of the leyaks. She leads an army of evil witches against the Barong, leader of the forces of good, and their battle is staged in the Barong dance as the eternal struggle between good and evil. Her name comes from an Old Javanese word meaning 'widow'.

long_description.id: Rangda digambarkan sebagai perempuan tua yang hampir telanjang, berambut panjang kusut, berpayudara menggantung, dan bercakar. Wajahnya berupa topeng bertaring dengan mata melotot dan lidah panjang yang menjulur. Dalam pertunjukan, ia bergerak liar seperti binatang dengan langkah melompat, sementara nyala api tampak di atas matanya yang melotot dan di sepanjang lidahnya.
long_description.en: Rangda is depicted as a mostly nude old woman with long unkempt hair, pendulous breasts and claws. Her face is a fanged, goggle-eyed mask with a long protruding tongue. In performance she moves wildly like an animal with a leaping gait, while flames rise above her bulging eyes and along her tongue.

long_description.id: Rangda dikaitkan dengan legenda Calon Arang, janda penyihir yang merusak Jawa pada masa pemerintahan Airlangga akhir abad ke-10, dan dengan legenda Mahendradatta, ratu Jawa yang diasingkan. Tafsiran lain menyebut Rangda berasal dari Mahendradatta, istri raja Bali Udayana dan ibu Airlangga, yang dikenal karena pengabdiannya pada pemujaan Durga di Bali.
long_description.en: Rangda is linked to the legend of Calon Arang, the widow-witch who wreaked havoc in Java during Airlangga's reign in the late 10th century, and to the legend of Mahendradatta, an exiled Javanese queen. Another interpretation derives Rangda from Mahendradatta, wife of the Balinese king Udayana and mother of Airlangga, known for her devotion to the cult of Durga in Bali.

long_description.id: Dalam Hindu Bali, Rangda dipandang sebagai perwujudan Durga dan pasangan Dewa Siwa, dengan wilayah kekuasaan di kuburan. Topeng sakral Rangda disimpan di pura dalem, lalu diarak saat upacara ulang tahun pura. Lontar Siwa Tattwa dan Lontar Usada Taru Premana menyebutnya perwujudan Dewi Durga di bumi dengan gelar Hyang Bherawi.
long_description.en: In Balinese Hinduism Rangda is seen as a manifestation of Durga and consort of the god Siwa, and her realm is the cemetery. Sacred Rangda masks are kept in village temples of the dead and brought out in procession for temple anniversary ceremonies. The Lontar Siwa Tattwa and Lontar Usada Taru Premana identify her as the goddess Durga on earth, with the title Hyang Bherawi.

long_description.id: Para peneliti menekankan bahwa Rangda lebih dari sekadar tokoh jahat. Dalam pertarungan yang dipentaskan setidaknya setahun sekali di desa-desa Bali, Rangda dikalahkan tetapi tidak pernah dibunuh, karena energi negatifnya hidup berdampingan dengan energi positif. Hubungan Rangda dan Barong dipahami melalui konsep Rwa Bhineda, filosofi Bali tentang keseimbangan dua kutub yang berlawanan.
long_description.en: Researchers stress that Rangda is more than a villain. In the battle reenacted at least once a year in Balinese villages, Rangda is defeated but never killed, because her negative energy coexists with the positive. The relationship between Rangda and Barong is understood through Rwa Bhineda, the Balinese philosophy of balance between two opposing poles.

cultural_context.id: Dalam Hindu Bali, upaya menjaga keseimbangan kekuatan yang berlawanan, seperti baik dan jahat, meresapi seluruh kehidupan, dan Rangda bersama Barong menjadi perwujudan keseimbangan itu dalam ritual dan pertunjukan.
cultural_context.en: In Balinese Hinduism the effort to keep opposing forces such as good and evil in balance pervades all of life, and Rangda and the Barong embody that balance in ritual and performance.

summary.id: Calon Arang, janda yang menguasai ilmu hitam, marah karena putrinya Ratna Manggali tidak mendapat suami. Ia mendatangkan banjir dan penyakit. Raja Airlangga meminta Empu Bharada menanganinya; muridnya Empu Bahula menikahi Ratna dan mengambil kitab mantra Calon Arang, lalu Calon Arang dikalahkan tanpa bantuan Durga.
summary.en: Calon Arang, a widow skilled in black magic, grew angry because her daughter Ratna Manggali could not find a husband. She brought flood and disease. King Airlangga asked Empu Bharada to deal with her; his disciple Empu Bahula married Ratna and took Calon Arang's book of spells, and without Durga's help Calon Arang was defeated.

claims.quote: Rangda (Balinese: ᬭᬗ᭄ᬤ) is the demon queen of the Leyaks in Bali, according to traditional Balinese mythology.

statement.id: Menurut mitologi tradisional Bali, Rangda (aksara Bali: ᬭᬗ᭄ᬤ) adalah ratu iblis para leak di Bali.
statement.en: According to traditional Balinese mythology, Rangda (Balinese: ᬭᬗ᭄ᬤ) is the demon queen of the leyaks in Bali.

claims.quote: the child-eating Rangda leads an army of evil witches against the leader of the forces of good — Barong. The battle between Barong and Rangda is featured in a Barong dance which represents the eternal battle between good and evil.

statement.id: Rangda pemakan anak memimpin pasukan penyihir jahat melawan Barong, pemimpin kekuatan baik; pertarungan mereka ditampilkan dalam tari Barong sebagai pertempuran abadi baik dan jahat.
statement.en: The child-eating Rangda leads evil witches against Barong, leader of the forces of good; their battle is shown in the Barong dance as the eternal struggle of good and evil.

claims.quote: Rangda is a term in old Javanese that means "widow".

statement.id: Rangda adalah istilah Jawa Kuno yang berarti janda.
statement.en: Rangda is an Old Javanese term meaning widow.

claims.quote: She is depicted as a mostly nude old woman, with long and unkempt hair, pendulous breasts, and claws. Her face is traditionally a horrifying fanged and goggle-eyed mask, with a long, protruding tongue.

statement.id: Rangda digambarkan sebagai perempuan tua hampir telanjang, berambut panjang kusut, berpayudara menggantung, bercakar, dengan topeng bertaring, bermata melotot, dan lidah panjang menjulur.
statement.en: Rangda is depicted as a mostly nude old woman with long unkempt hair, pendulous breasts and claws, with a fanged, goggle-eyed mask and long protruding tongue.

claims.quote: Rangda is known as a Leyak queen, the incarnation of Calon Arang, the legendary witch that wreaked havoc in ancient Java during the reign of Airlangga in the late 10th century.

statement.id: Rangda dikenal sebagai ratu leak, penjelmaan Calon Arang, penyihir legendaris yang merusak Jawa kuno pada masa Airlangga akhir abad ke-10.
statement.en: Rangda is known as a leyak queen, incarnation of Calon Arang, the legendary witch who wreaked havoc in ancient Java under Airlangga in the late 10th century.

claims.quote: Rangda was linked to the legend of Calon Arang and also the legend of the divorced and exiled Javanese queen Mahendradatta.

statement.id: Rangda dikaitkan dengan legenda Calon Arang dan legenda Mahendradatta, ratu Jawa yang diceraikan dan diasingkan.
statement.en: Rangda is linked to the legend of Calon Arang and to that of Mahendradatta, a divorced and exiled Javanese queen.

claims.quote: Rangda’s name means “widow” in Balinese, and it comes from a legendary Javanese-Balinese tale, the 12th-century Calonarang.

statement.id: Nama Rangda berarti janda dalam bahasa Bali dan berasal dari kisah legendaris Jawa-Bali abad ke-12, Calonarang.
statement.en: Rangda's name means widow in Balinese and comes from the 12th-century Javanese-Balinese tale Calonarang.

claims.quote: She was the wife of Balinese king Udayana and Airlangga's mother. Mahendradatta is known for her devotion to the cult of Durga in Bali.

statement.id: Mahendradatta, yang oleh tafsiran lain dianggap asal Rangda, adalah istri raja Bali Udayana dan ibu Airlangga, dikenal karena pengabdiannya pada pemujaan Durga di Bali.
statement.en: Mahendradatta, from whom other interpretations derive Rangda, was wife of the Balinese king Udayana and Airlangga's mother, known for her devotion to Durga in Bali.

claims.quote: It is said that Calon Arang was a widow, who had mastered the art of black magic, who often damaged farmers' crops and caused disease to come. She had a daughter, named Ratna Manggali, who, though beautiful, could not get a husband because people were afraid of her mother.

statement.id: Calon Arang adalah janda penguasa ilmu hitam yang merusak panen dan mendatangkan penyakit; putrinya, Ratna Manggali, tidak mendapat suami karena orang takut pada ibunya.
statement.en: Calon Arang was a widow skilled in black magic who damaged crops and brought disease; her daughter Ratna Manggali could not find a husband because people feared her mother.

claims.quote: In the unique form of Hinduism practiced in Bali, Rangda is the supreme manifestation of the evil aspects of power.

statement.id: Dalam Hindu Bali, Rangda adalah perwujudan tertinggi aspek jahat dari kekuatan.
statement.en: In Balinese Hinduism, Rangda is the supreme manifestation of the evil aspects of power.

claims.quote: her wild and untamed energy is made visible as she moves animal-like, with reckless gestures and a leaping gait.

statement.id: Dalam pertunjukan, Rangda bergerak liar seperti binatang dengan gerak sembrono dan langkah melompat.
statement.en: In performance Rangda moves wildly like an animal with reckless gestures and a leaping gait.

claims.quote: As the manifestation of the great Hindu goddess Durga, Rangda is the consort of the god Siwa the destroyer (known as Shiva in Sanskrit). Her realm is the cemetery, and sacred masks of Rangda are kept in the nearby village temples of the dead

statement.id: Sebagai perwujudan Durga, Rangda adalah pasangan Dewa Siwa; wilayahnya adalah kuburan, dan topeng sakralnya disimpan di pura desa untuk orang mati (pura dalem).
statement.en: As a manifestation of Durga, Rangda is consort of the god Siwa; her realm is the cemetery, and her sacred masks are kept in village temples of the dead.

claims.quote: In the ensuing battle—one that is reenacted at least once a year in villages throughout Bali—Rangda is defeated but never killed, since her negative energy co-exists with the positive.

statement.id: Dalam pertarungan yang dipentaskan setidaknya setahun sekali di desa-desa Bali, Rangda dikalahkan tetapi tidak pernah dibunuh, karena energi negatifnya hidup berdampingan dengan yang positif.
statement.en: In the battle reenacted at least once a year in Balinese villages, Rangda is defeated but never killed, since her negative energy coexists with the positive.

claims.quote: However, further research shows that Rangda’s role in Bali is more than an artistic device; she also serves an important religious function as a sacred symbol

statement.id: Penelitian menunjukkan peran Rangda di Bali lebih dari sekadar perangkat seni; ia juga berfungsi religius sebagai simbol sakral.
statement.en: Research shows Rangda's role in Bali is more than an artistic device; she also serves a religious function as a sacred symbol.

claims.quote: Rwa Bhineda, a Balinese philosophy that emphasizes the balance between two opposing polarities, finds its explicit manifestation in the relationship between Rangda and Barong.

statement.id: Rwa Bhineda, filosofi Bali tentang keseimbangan dua kutub berlawanan, tampak nyata dalam hubungan Rangda dan Barong.
statement.en: Rwa Bhineda, a Balinese philosophy of balance between two opposing poles, is explicitly manifested in the relationship of Rangda and Barong.

claims.quote: This view is reinforced by the Lontar Siwa Tattwa and Lontar Usada Taru Premana, which identify Rangda as the embodiment of the goddess Durga on earth with the title Hyang Bherawi

statement.id: Lontar Siwa Tattwa dan Lontar Usada Taru Premana menyebut Rangda perwujudan Dewi Durga di bumi dengan gelar Hyang Bherawi.
statement.en: The Lontar Siwa Tattwa and Lontar Usada Taru Premana identify Rangda as the goddess Durga on earth with the title Hyang Bherawi.

claims.quote: In Balinese Hinduism, the struggle to maintain or return the cosmological balance of opposing forces, such as good and evil or life and death, permeates all of life.

statement.id: Dalam Hindu Bali, upaya menjaga atau memulihkan keseimbangan kosmologis kekuatan yang berlawanan, seperti baik dan jahat, meresapi seluruh kehidupan.
statement.en: In Balinese Hinduism, the struggle to maintain or restore the cosmological balance of opposing forces, such as good and evil, permeates all of life.

claims.quote: King Airlangga, who had heard of this matter, then asked for his advisor, Empu Bharada, to deal with this problem. Empu Bharada then sent his disciple, Empu Bahula, to be married to Ratna.

statement.id: Raja Airlangga meminta penasihatnya, Empu Bharada, menangani masalah ini; Empu Bharada mengutus muridnya, Empu Bahula, untuk menikahi Ratna.
statement.en: King Airlangga asked his advisor Empu Bharada to deal with the problem; Empu Bharada sent his disciple Empu Bahula to marry Ratna.

claims.quote: One day, this book was found by Empu Bahula, who turned it over to Empu Bharada. As soon as Calon Arang knew that the book had been stolen, she became angry and decided to fight Empu Bharada. Without the help of Durga, Calon Arang was defeated.

statement.id: Empu Bahula menemukan kitab mantra Calon Arang dan menyerahkannya kepada Empu Bharada; Calon Arang yang marah melawan Empu Bharada dan kalah tanpa bantuan Durga.
statement.en: Empu Bahula found Calon Arang's book and gave it to Empu Bharada; the angry Calon Arang fought Empu Bharada and, without Durga's help, was defeated.

claims.quote: The next day, a great flood engulfed the village and many people died. Disease also appeared.

statement.id: Keesokan harinya banjir besar melanda desa, banyak orang meninggal, dan penyakit muncul.
statement.en: The next day a great flood engulfed the village, many died, and disease appeared.

short_description.id: Shachihoko adalah makhluk legenda berkepala harimau dan bertubuh ikan; hiasan berbentuknya dipasang di atap kastel sebagai penolak api.
short_description.en: Shachihoko is a legendary tiger-headed, fish-bodied creature whose roof ornaments were believed to protect castles from fire.

long_description.id: Shachihoko, yang juga disebut shachi, digambarkan sebagai makhluk berkepala harimau dan bertubuh ikan. Menurut cerita rakyat, ia dapat menyemburkan air dari mulut untuk memadamkan api. Karena kepercayaan itu, bentuknya dipasang sebagai hiasan ujung bubungan di banyak atap kastel.
long_description.en: Shachihoko, also called shachi, is described with a tiger’s head and a fish’s body. Folklore gives it the power to spray water from its mouth to extinguish fires. Belief in its protection led to ornaments shaped like it on many castle roofs.

long_description.id: Hiasan ini sering dibuat berpasangan sebagai jantan dan betina. Pada pasangan di Kastel Matsumoto, mulut jantan terbuka dan mulut betina tertutup; keterangan resmi mengaitkannya dengan bunyi awal dan akhir dalam tradisi agama. Sepasang hiasan yang kini dipamerkan di sana dilepas dari atap saat perbaikan pada 1950-an, dan inskripsi penyangganya mengisyaratkan pemasangan pada 1843. Kastel Nagoya juga terkenal dengan shachihoko keemasan di atapnya.
long_description.en: The ornaments often come in male and female pairs. In a pair at Matsumoto Castle, the male has an open mouth and the female a closed one; the official account links them to sounds symbolizing beginning and end in religious tradition. A displayed pair was taken from the roof during repairs in the 1950s, and inscriptions suggest installation in 1843. Nagoya Castle also has golden shachihoko on its roof.
