text.id: Pemujaan nat lebih tua daripada agama Buddha di Myanmar; daftar resmi 37 Nat Agung ditetapkan pada abad ke-11.
text.en: Nat worship predates Buddhism in Myanmar; the official list of 37 Great Nats was fixed in the 11th century.

short_description.id: Nat adalah roh yang dipuja di Myanmar bersama agama Buddha, baik roh alam maupun manusia yang didewakan setelah mati, dengan 37 Nat Agung sebagai jajaran resminya.
short_description.en: Nats are spirits venerated in Myanmar alongside Buddhism, either nature spirits or humans deified after death, with the 37 Great Nats as their official pantheon.

long_description.id: Nat adalah roh serupa dewa yang dipuja di Myanmar dan negara-negara sekitarnya, berdampingan dengan agama Buddha. Kepercayaan Myanmar membedakan dua jenis nat: nat sein, yaitu manusia yang didewakan setelah meninggal, dan roh alam seperti roh air dan pohon. Sebagian besar dari 37 Nat Agung adalah manusia yang meninggal secara kejam. Selain 37 Nat Agung, ada ratusan nat lain yang dipuja lewat upacara lokal dan daerah.
long_description.en: Nats are god-like spirits venerated in Myanmar and neighbouring countries alongside Buddhism. Burmese belief distinguishes two kinds: nat sein, humans deified after death, and nature spirits such as those of water and trees. Most of the 37 Great Nats were humans who met violent deaths. Beyond the 37 Great Nats, hundreds of other nats are supplicated through local and regional ceremonies.

long_description.id: Setiap desa di Myanmar memiliki kuil kecil untuk nat penjaga desa, dan rumah-rumah juga punya tempat pemujaan nat, biasanya berupa buah kelapa yang digantung di sudut rumah. Masyarakat pedesaan juga percaya pada roh penjaga hutan dan gunung, dan kepercayaan bahwa pohon besar dihuni roh pohon membuat orang enggan menebangnya sembarangan. Ada pula nat penjaga tanah, kota, dan jalan; Min Mahagiri, misalnya, adalah pemimpin jajaran 37 sekaligus pelindung rumah tangga.
long_description.en: Every Burmese village has a small shrine for its guardian nat, and houses also keep a nat shrine, usually a coconut hung in a corner of the house. Rural communities also believe in forest and mountain guardian spirits, and the belief that large trees house tree spirits makes people reluctant to fell them indiscriminately. There are also guardians of land, towns and roads; Min Mahagiri, for instance, leads the 37 and also protects the household.

long_description.id: Pemujaan nat lebih tua daripada agama Buddha di Myanmar. Raja Anawrahta dari Bagan menetapkan jajaran resmi 37 Nat Agung dan membiarkan nat ditempatkan di kuil Buddha agar rakyat tertarik pada agama barunya. Para akademisi berbeda pendapat apakah agama Buddha Myanmar dan pemujaan roh adalah dua hal terpisah atau satu agama. Angka 37 sendiri adalah urutan mistis yang sering dipakai dalam sejarah Myanmar sejak masa Bagan. Penetapan itu juga ditafsirkan sebagai upaya menegakkan dominasi Bamar di lembah Irrawaddy.
long_description.en: Nat worship predates Buddhism in Myanmar. King Anawrahta of Bagan fixed the official pantheon of 37 Great Nats and allowed nats into temples to draw people to his new religion. Scholars disagree on whether Burmese Buddhism and spirit worship are separate or a single religion. The number 37 itself is a mystical ordering used often in Burmese history since the Bagan period. That formalization has also been read as establishing Bamar supremacy in the Irrawaddy valley.

long_description.id: Nat digambarkan punya sifat, keinginan, dan kebutuhan seperti manusia, termasuk keinginan yang dianggap tidak bermoral dalam ajaran Buddha arus utama. Dalam festival nat pwè, para nat kadaw (medium roh) menari dan menjadi wadah nat, sementara pengunjung menari diiringi orkestra hsaing waing dan kerasukan nat.
long_description.en: Nats are given human characteristics, wants and needs, including desires considered immoral in mainstream Buddhism. At nat pwè festivals, nat kadaws (spirit mediums) dance and embody the nats, while participants dance to hsaing waing orchestra music, possessed by the nats.

long_description.id: Gunung Popa, gunung api mati di dekat Bagan, adalah tempat ziarah nat terpenting di Myanmar. Di biara Taung Kalat, peziarah menaiki 777 anak tangga untuk meletakkan persembahan di kuil-kuil nat; persembahannya disesuaikan dengan nat yang dituju, misalnya wiski untuk Min Kyawzwa.
long_description.en: Mount Popa, an extinct volcano near Bagan, is Myanmar's most important nat pilgrimage site. At Taung Kalat monastery, pilgrims climb 777 stairs to leave offerings at nat shrines, chosen to suit the nat in question, such as whisky for Min Kyawzwa.

cultural_context.id: Kepercayaan pada roh penjaga hutan dan gunung berfungsi, sampai batas tertentu, sebagai penghalang perusakan lingkungan, karena menebang pohon besar diyakini mendatangkan murka nat.
cultural_context.en: Belief in forest and mountain guardian spirits acts, up to a point, as a deterrent against environmental destruction, because felling large trees is believed to bring the nat's wrath.

claims.quote: The nats (နတ်; MLCTS: nat; IPA: [naʔ]) are god-like spirits venerated in Myanmar and neighbouring countries in conjunction with Buddhism. They are divided between the 37 Great Nats who were given that status by King Anawrahta

statement.id: Nat (နတ်) adalah roh serupa dewa yang dipuja di Myanmar dan negara sekitarnya bersama agama Buddha; ada 37 Nat Agung yang statusnya diberikan Raja Anawrahta.
statement.en: Nats (နတ်) are god-like spirits venerated in Myanmar and neighbouring countries alongside Buddhism; the 37 Great Nats received that status from King Anawrahta.

claims.quote: Most of the 37 Great Nats were human beings who met violent deaths. There are two types of nats in Burmese Belief: nat sein (နတ်စိမ်း), which are humans that were deified after their deaths, and all other nats, which are spirits of nature (spirits of water, trees etc.).

statement.id: Sebagian besar 37 Nat Agung adalah manusia yang mati secara kejam; ada dua jenis nat: nat sein (manusia yang didewakan setelah mati) dan roh alam seperti roh air dan pohon.
statement.en: Most of the 37 Great Nats were humans who died violently; there are two kinds of nats: nat sein (humans deified after death) and nature spirits such as those of water and trees.

claims.quote: Every Burmese village has a nat kun (နတ်ကွန်း) or nat sin (နတ်စင်), which essentially serves as a shrine to the village guardian nat called the ywa saung nat (ရွာစောင့်နတ်). Individual houses also have a shrine to a nat, usually a coconut is hung on a corner of the house

statement.id: Setiap desa Myanmar punya kuil untuk nat penjaga desa (ywa saung nat), dan rumah-rumah punya tempat pemujaan nat, biasanya kelapa yang digantung di sudut rumah.
statement.en: Every Burmese village has a shrine for the village guardian nat (ywa saung nat), and houses have a nat shrine, usually a coconut hung in a corner of the house.

claims.quote: Worship of nats predates Buddhism in Burma. With the arrival of Buddhism, however, the nats were syncretically merged with Buddhism.

statement.id: Pemujaan nat lebih tua daripada agama Buddha di Myanmar; setelah Buddha datang, nat dilebur secara sinkretis dengan agama Buddha.
statement.en: Nat worship predates Buddhism in Burma; after Buddhism arrived, the nats were syncretically merged with it.

claims.quote: Anawrahta used traditional nat spirits to attract people to his new religion.

statement.id: Anawrahta memakai roh nat tradisional untuk menarik rakyat ke agama barunya.
statement.en: Anawrahta used traditional nat spirits to attract people to his new religion.

claims.quote: The widespread traditional belief among rural communities that there are forest guardian spirits called taw saung nats (တောစောင့်နတ်) and mountain guardian spirits called taung saung nats (တောင်စောင့်နတ်) appears to act as a deterrent against environmental destruction, up to a point.

statement.id: Kepercayaan pedesaan pada roh penjaga hutan (taw saung nat) dan gunung (taung saung nat) tampaknya menjadi penghalang perusakan lingkungan sampai batas tertentu.
statement.en: The rural belief in forest (taw saung nat) and mountain (taung saung nat) guardian spirits appears to deter environmental destruction up to a point.

claims.quote: The most important nat pilgrimage site in Burma is Mount Popa, an extinct volcano with numerous temples and relic sites atop a 1,300-metre-tall (4,300 ft) mountain located near Bagan in central Burma.

statement.id: Tempat ziarah nat terpenting di Myanmar adalah Gunung Popa, gunung api mati setinggi 1.300 meter di dekat Bagan.
statement.en: Burma's most important nat pilgrimage site is Mount Popa, a 1,300-metre extinct volcano near Bagan.

claims.quote: Nats are ascribed human characteristics, wants, and needs; they are flawed, having desires considered derogatory and immoral in mainstream Buddhism.

statement.id: Nat dianggap punya sifat, keinginan, dan kebutuhan manusia, termasuk keinginan yang dianggap tidak bermoral dalam Buddha arus utama.
statement.en: Nats are given human characteristics, wants and needs, including desires considered immoral in mainstream Buddhism.

claims.quote: During a nat pwè, which is a festival during which nats are propitiated, nat kadaws (နတ်ကတော် "wife of the spirit", i.e. "medium, shaman") dance and embody the nats.

statement.id: Dalam nat pwè, festival untuk menenangkan nat, para nat kadaw (medium roh) menari dan menjadi wadah nat.
statement.en: At a nat pwè, a festival to propitiate nats, nat kadaws (spirit mediums) dance and embody the nats.

claims.quote: Taungbyone, north of Mandalay in Madaya Township, is another major site with the festival held each year starting on the eleventh waxing day and including the full moon in the month Wagaung (August). Yadanagu at Amarapura, held a week later in honour of Popa Medaw

statement.id: Taungbyone di utara Mandalay adalah situs festival nat besar setiap bulan Wagaung; festival Yadanagu di Amarapura diadakan seminggu kemudian untuk menghormati Popa Medaw.
statement.en: Taungbyone north of Mandalay is a major nat festival site each Wagaung; Yadanagu at Amarapura is held a week later in honour of Popa Medaw.

claims.quote: The nat kadaws as an independent profession made their appearance in the latter half of the 19th century as spirit mediums, and nat kannahs are more of an urban phenomenon which evolved to satisfy the need of people who had migrated from the countryside to towns and cities

statement.id: Nat kadaw muncul sebagai profesi mandiri pada paruh kedua abad ke-19, dan nat kannah lebih merupakan gejala kota bagi pendatang dari desa.
statement.en: Nat kadaws emerged as an independent profession in the latter half of the 19th century, and nat kannahs are more an urban phenomenon for migrants from the countryside.

claims.quote: Academic opinions vary as to whether Burmese Buddhism and Burmese spirit worship are two separate entities or merged into a single religion.

statement.id: Pendapat akademik berbeda apakah Buddha Myanmar dan pemujaan roh Myanmar adalah dua hal terpisah atau satu agama.
statement.en: Academic opinions differ on whether Burmese Buddhism and spirit worship are separate or a single religion.

claims.quote: The 37 Great Nats, first recognized during the 11th century, were once high-status humans. All but one—Thagyamin, the lucky sod—perished in violent or painful circumstances. Snake bites, leprosy, beheading, forceful immolation, drowning, and falling off a swing are but a few of the myriad ways in which they died.

statement.id: 37 Nat Agung, yang diakui sejak abad ke-11, dulunya manusia berstatus tinggi; semua kecuali Thagyamin mati secara kejam atau menyakitkan, misalnya gigitan ular, kusta, dipenggal, dibakar, tenggelam, atau jatuh dari ayunan.
statement.en: The 37 Great Nats, recognized since the 11th century, were once high-status humans; all but Thagyamin died violently or painfully, e.g. snake bites, leprosy, beheading, immolation, drowning or falling off a swing.

claims.quote: Pilgrims climb the 777 stairs of Taung Kalat—barefoot and dodging monkey dung along the way—to leave offerings at the colorful shrines located at the summit. Money is the standard gift, but other items are acceptable according to the nat in question. Min Kyawzwa, a nat known for his alcoholism and antagonistic personality, is regularly honored with bottles of whisky.

statement.id: Peziarah menaiki 777 anak tangga Taung Kalat untuk meletakkan persembahan di kuil-kuil puncaknya; uang adalah persembahan umum, tetapi barang lain disesuaikan dengan nat, misalnya wiski untuk Min Kyawzwa.
statement.en: Pilgrims climb Taung Kalat's 777 stairs to leave offerings at its summit shrines; money is standard, but other items suit the nat, such as whisky for Min Kyawzwa.

claims.quote: Guardian Spirits of tree, mountain, land house, village, town, country, roads. Some Nat Spirits overlap categories: Min Mahagiri is a leader of the 37 Pantheon and also a protector Nat of the household.

statement.id: Ada roh penjaga pohon, gunung, tanah, rumah, desa, kota, negara, dan jalan; sebagian nat masuk beberapa golongan, misalnya Min Mahagiri, pemimpin jajaran 37 sekaligus pelindung rumah.
statement.en: There are guardian spirits of trees, mountains, land, houses, villages, towns, the country and roads; some overlap, e.g. Min Mahagiri, leader of the 37 and protector of the household.

claims.quote: Actually, throughout Myanmar, there are hundreds and hundreds of different “Nat” Spirits who are supplicated through local and regional ceremonies (pwe)

statement.id: Di seluruh Myanmar ada ratusan nat berbeda yang dipuja lewat upacara lokal dan daerah (pwe).
statement.en: Throughout Myanmar there are hundreds of different nats supplicated through local and regional ceremonies (pwe).

claims.quote: The number “37” is used as a mystical ordering (said to originate from Hindu cosmology) used frequently throughout Burmese history since the Bagan period.

statement.id: Angka 37 adalah urutan mistis, konon dari kosmologi Hindu, yang sering dipakai dalam sejarah Myanmar sejak masa Bagan.
statement.en: The number 37 is a mystical ordering, said to come from Hindu cosmology, used often in Burmese history since the Bagan period.

claims.quote: The formalizing of the official 37 Great Nats by King Anawrahta (1044–1077) of Bagan, has been interpreted as Burmanisation and establishment of Bamar supremacy in the Irrawaddy valley

statement.id: Penetapan resmi 37 Nat Agung oleh Raja Anawrahta (1044–1077) dari Bagan ditafsirkan sebagai burmanisasi dan penegakan dominasi Bamar di lembah Irrawaddy.
statement.en: The formalizing of the 37 Great Nats by King Anawrahta (1044–1077) of Bagan has been interpreted as Burmanisation and the establishment of Bamar supremacy in the Irrawaddy valley.

claims.quote: Nat Spirits who are deceased humans still in limbo between lives, stuck in their regret or bitterness. THESE are the predominant Pantheon of 37, called “Nat Sein” – those who died a violent death

statement.id: Nat yang merupakan manusia yang telah meninggal dan masih terjebak di antara kehidupan disebut nat sein, yaitu mereka yang mati secara kejam; merekalah sebagian besar jajaran 37.
statement.en: Nats who are deceased humans still in limbo between lives are called nat sein, those who died a violent death; they make up most of the 37.

short_description.id: Ōyamatsumi adalah kami pegunungan dalam tradisi Jepang, dengan kisah asal-usul berbeda dalam Kojiki dan Nihongi.
short_description.en: Ōyamatsumi is a mountain kami of Japanese tradition whose origins differ between the Kojiki and Nihongi.

long_description.id: Ōyamatsumi adalah kami yang namanya terkait dengan roh penghuni gunung; ensiklopedia Shinto menafsirkannya sebagai dewa agung yang menguasai pegunungan. Kojiki menyebutnya salah satu dewa yang muncul ketika Izanagi dan Izanami melahirkan daratan. Sebuah varian dalam Nihongi justru menyebutnya terlahir dari salah satu bagian Kagutsuchi setelah dipotong Izanagi. Kedua kisah itu dicatat sebagai versi asal-usul yang berbeda.
long_description.en: Ōyamatsumi is a kami whose name relates to a spirit dwelling in a mountain; a Shinto encyclopedia explains it as a great deity with authority over mountains. The Kojiki names him among the deities born when Izanagi and Izanami produced the land. An alternate account in the Nihongi says he arose from a part of Kagutsuchi after Izanagi cut him up. These are distinct accounts of his origin.

long_description.id: Kuil untuk kami bernama Ōyamatsumi terdapat di berbagai tempat di Jepang. Dalam kepercayaan rakyat, nama itu juga dapat dipakai bagi kami suatu gunung atau roh orang yang meninggal di pegunungan. Sebuah kuil di Toba memujanya sebagai dewa gunung dan laut; menurut catatan setempat, kuil itu dipindahkan ketika pembangunan Kastel Toba berlangsung. Dua festival musim semi di sana menampilkan tarian berkostum serta arak-arakan mikoshi.
long_description.en: Shrines to kami named Ōyamatsumi are found across Japan. In folk religion, the name can also denote the kami of a particular mountain or the spirit of someone who died there. A shrine in Toba honors him as a deity of mountains and seas; a local account says it was moved during construction of Toba Castle. Two spring festivals there include a costumed dance and a mikoshi procession.

claims.quote: The term yamatsumi means a spirit dwelling within a mountain, with the result that the name Ōyamatsumi means a great deity with jurisdiction over mountains.

statement.id: Nama Ōyamatsumi mengacu pada dewa yang menguasai pegunungan.
statement.en: The name Ōyamatsumi refers to a great deity over mountains.

claims.quote: According to Kojiki, one of the deities produced as Izanagi no mikoto and Izanami no mikoto gave birth to the land

statement.id: Menurut Kojiki, ia lahir saat Izanagi dan Izanami melahirkan daratan.
statement.en: According to the Kojiki, he arose as Izanagi and Izanami produced the land.

claims.quote: According to an "alternate writing" transmitted by Nihongi, Ōyamatsumi was produced from one of the three pieces into which Kagutsuchi was cut by Izanagi.

statement.id: Varian Nihongi menyebut ia berasal dari potongan Kagutsuchi.
statement.en: A Nihongi variant says he arose from a piece of Kagutsuchi.

claims.quote: Shrines to kami with this name can be found throughout Japan.

statement.id: Kuil untuk kami bernama Ōyamatsumi tersebar di Jepang.
statement.en: Shrines to kami with this name are found throughout Japan.

claims.quote: In Japanese folk religion, the kami of any given mountain is sometimes called Ōyamatsumi, as is the spirit of someone who has died within the mountains; in many cases, cairns of stones are erected as a place of worship.

statement.id: Dalam kepercayaan rakyat Jepang, nama itu dapat menunjuk kami suatu gunung atau roh orang yang meninggal di pegunungan.
statement.en: In Japanese folk religion, the name can mean a mountain kami or the spirit of someone who died in the mountains.

claims.quote: this shrine to Oyamazumi, the kami (Shinto deity) of mountains and seas, was located on the hilltop where construction was taking place.

statement.id: Kuil di Toba memuja Oyamazumi sebagai dewa gunung dan laut.
statement.en: The Toba shrine worships Oyamazumi as a deity of mountains and seas.

claims.quote: After many incidents of the stone walls and foundations collapsing, he had the shrine moved to its current location. The problems ceased, and Yoshitaka was able to complete construction of the castle.

statement.id: Menurut catatan setempat, kuil dipindahkan saat pembangunan kastel setelah fondasi dan tembok berulang kali runtuh.
statement.en: The local account says the shrine was moved after repeated collapses during castle construction.

claims.quote: Oyamazumi is known for two spring festivals: One features a dance where performers dress up as traditional costumes of lions and tengu, legendary kami with distinctive long noses.

statement.id: Dua festival musim semi untuk Oyamazumi mencakup tarian dengan kostum singa dan tengu.
statement.en: Two spring festivals for Oyamazumi include a dance with lion and tengu costumes.

claims.quote: In the other, townsfolk carry a mikoshi (portable shrine) around town accompanied by traditional music.

statement.id: Festival lain menampilkan arak-arakan mikoshi diiringi musik tradisional.
statement.en: Another festival includes a mikoshi procession with traditional music.

summary.id: Dalam Kojiki, ia lahir ketika Izanagi dan Izanami melahirkan daratan.
summary.en: In the Kojiki he arose as Izanagi and Izanami produced the land.

summary.id: Dalam varian Nihongi, ia muncul dari bagian Kagutsuchi yang dipotong Izanagi.
summary.en: In an alternate Nihongi account, he arose from a piece of Kagutsuchi cut by Izanagi.

short_description.id: Tenjin adalah nama ilahi bagi Sugawara no Michizane yang dipuja sebagai pelindung ilmu pengetahuan setelah wafat dalam pembuangan.
short_description.en: Tenjin is the deified Sugawara no Michizane, revered as a patron of scholarship after his death in exile.

long_description.id: Tenjin mula-mula berarti “dewa langit”, tetapi kemudian terutama merujuk pada roh cendekiawan istana Sugawara no Michizane. Ia dibuang karena intrik politik dan wafat dalam pembuangan. Kemudian bencana dikaitkan dengan rohnya yang murka; istana memulihkan kedudukannya secara anumerta dan ia akhirnya didewakan. Dalam kepercayaan sesudahnya, ia dihormati sebagai pelindung ilmu pengetahuan.
long_description.en: Tenjin originally meant “heavenly god” but later referred chiefly to the spirit of the court scholar Sugawara no Michizane. Political intrigue sent him into exile, where he died. Later disasters were attributed to his angry spirit; the court restored his rank after death and he was eventually deified. In later devotion he is revered as a patron of scholarship.

long_description.id: Istilah tenjin juga pernah dipakai untuk dewa langit sebelum pemujaan Michizane berkembang, sehingga makna awalnya perlu dibedakan dari tokoh ini. Sebuah ensiklopedia menjelaskan bahwa sosok Tenjin memadukan roh Michizane dengan gambaran dewa guntur dan beberapa unsur keagamaan lain. Kuil Kitano Tenmangū didedikasikan kepadanya pada 947; pemujaannya kemudian menyebar lewat kuil cabang. Kini para pelajar juga mendatanginya berkaitan dengan ujian masuk sekolah dan universitas.
long_description.en: The word tenjin was also used for heavenly deities before devotion to Michizane developed, so its earlier sense should be distinguished from this figure. An encyclopedia describes Tenjin as combining Michizane’s spirit with a thunder deity and other religious elements. Kitano Tenmangū was dedicated to him in 947, followed by branch shrines. Students today also turn to him in connection with school and university entrance exams.

cultural_context.id: Tenjin dipuja sebagai pelindung ilmu pengetahuan di kuil-kuil, dan pelajar mendatangi kuilnya menjelang ujian.
cultural_context.en: Tenjin is venerated as a patron of scholarship, and students visit his shrine when preparing for examinations.

claims.quote: Originally meant "Heavenly God," but later came to refer exclusively to the spirit of courtier-scholar Sugawara Michizane (845-903).

statement.id: Tenjin semula berarti dewa langit tetapi kemudian merujuk pada roh Sugawara no Michizane.
statement.en: Tenjin originally meant heavenly god but later referred to Sugawara Michizane’s spirit.

claims.quote: A victim of political intrigue, Michizane was sent into exile but continued to protest his innocence through poetry until his death.

statement.id: Michizane dibuang akibat intrik politik dan meninggal dalam pembuangan.
statement.en: Michizane was exiled after political intrigue and died in exile.

claims.quote: His angry spirit was later judged to be the source of a series of disasters, and so he was posthumously pardoned, given a promotion in court rank, and ultimately deified.

statement.id: Serangkaian bencana dikaitkan dengan rohnya, lalu ia diampuni, dinaikkan pangkatnya, dan didewakan setelah wafat.
statement.en: Disasters were attributed to his spirit, followed by posthumous pardon, promotion, and deification.

claims.quote: He is revered as the patron saint of scholarship at such shrines as the Dazaifu Tenmangû in Fukuoka Prefecture and Kitano Tenjin shrines throughout Japan.

statement.id: Tenjin dihormati sebagai pelindung ilmu pengetahuan di kuil-kuil Jepang.
statement.en: Tenjin is revered as a patron of scholarship at shrines across Japan.

claims.quote: The use of the term "tenjin" however, predates the ninth century. In ancient China the expression "heavenly deities and earthly deities" (Tenjin chigi" 天神地祇) existed and subsequently in Japan the same characters were applied to the words "Amatsukami" and "Kunitsukami".

statement.id: Istilah tenjin telah dipakai sebelum pemujaan Michizane dan pernah menunjuk konsep dewa langit.
statement.en: The term tenjin predates Michizane’s cult and once denoted heavenly deities.

claims.quote: The kami Tenman Daijizai Tenjin is a combination of the tenjin "thunder deity" (raijin) who rules the weather, Michizane's "vengeful spirit" (goryō ), a Chinese deity for whom oxen were killed and offered, the esoteric Buddhist (Mikkyō) "Dharma protector deity" (gohōjin), and the mythological Amatsukami (Tenjin).

statement.id: Sosok Tenjin memadukan roh Michizane dengan dewa guntur dan unsur keagamaan lain.
statement.en: The figure of Tenjin combines Michizane’s spirit with a thunder deity and other religious elements.

claims.quote: This shrine was dedicated to noted scholar and poet Sugawara-no-Michizane (posthumously named Tenjin) in 947. It was revered by the court and the shogunate and spawned many branch shrines along with temple schools throughout the country.

statement.id: Kitano Tenmangū didedikasikan kepada Michizane pada 947 dan memunculkan kuil cabang.
statement.en: Kitano Tenmangū was dedicated to Michizane in 947 and gave rise to branch shrines.

claims.quote: Tenjin is now regarded as the deity of scholastic studies and is extremely popular with students preparing for high school or university entrance examinations.

statement.id: Pelajar yang menghadapi ujian masuk sekolah atau universitas menghormati Tenjin.
statement.en: Tenjin is popular with students preparing for school or university entrance exams.
